docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The handling of information security incidents is treated as a separate element of the IT Incident Management Plan [2] and Network Incident Management Plan [11] given the considerably more targeted and confidential nature of information security incidents. Currently there is a definite focus on Data Protection and The Electronic Communications Security Measures Regulations 2022 due to the prevailing compliance efforts, though not at the expense of generic applicability.

The objectives of Incident Management are:

  • Identify Incidents as early as possible to limit the impact on Community Fibre's information assets and clients.

  • Isolate the affected processes and / or systems to prevent further spread within the company.

  • Enable evidence to be gathered in accordance with company or legal requirements to enable the enforcement of formal disciplinary procedures and criminal proceedings if appropriate.

  • Maintain information on incidents to enable trend analysis to be undertaken.

  • Refine policies and procedures as necessary to reduce exposures.

  • Ensure that any new risk reduction measures identified as part of the investigation of an Incident are discussed and where appropriate, implemented.

  • Provide feedback into the threat assessments for the company.

Elements of the following sources of Incident Response requirements have been integrated (it [should]{.underline} be the case that further coverage is delivered as a result of feedback during live operation):

  • Data Protection requirement within reference [3]

  • NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF) v3.1 [12]

  • Telecommunications Security Code of Practice [13]

  • NIST SP 800-35 reference, see reference [4]

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The Security Incident Response Plan is applicable to all Community Fibre employees (staff, contracted third parties and agents of Community Fibre who have access to Community Fibre's systems, networks or information). It applies to all networks systems and systems that store, hold, process or transmit critical Community Fibre data.

Information Security is the responsibility of every employee and with your help and co-operation we can all contribute to making Community Fibre a safe and secure working environment.

Community Fibre staff should be aware that any breach of these responsibilities may result in disciplinary action and possible dismissal. Contractors, associates, temporary and service provider staff, and other persons who have been authorised to use Community Fibre Information Assets, must be aware that failure to comply with the requirements of this Framework may result in termination of contracts, contractual penalties and/or legal action, depending on the circumstances.

Community Fibre have partnered with ANS for a managed Security Operations Service. This service augments and extends our incident detection and response capabilities and provide expert knowledge that would otherwise have been difficult to build and implement.

Further responsibilities are placed on specific members of Community Fibre staff for the management of Incidents and Weaknesses once they have been reported.

docs.title: What Constitutes an Incident?
docs.text:
In a wider context, an Incident is defined as any event or action occurring within Community Fibre that results in a compromise of financial or information assets, the communications infrastructure and IT services or equipment, or in harm to people, either within Community Fibre or one of our clients.

A Weakness is a situation where there is potential for an Incident to occur but where no Incident has yet occurred.

Incidents are the result of errors in the management systems, failures in IT or network infrastructure or they might be caused by human error. All Incidents should be recorded, even if the cause of Incidents may be apparent and might be addressed without the need for further investigation.

docs.title: Information Security Incidents
docs.text:
An Information Security Incident is defined as an event that compromises the Confidentiality, Integrity or Availability of one or more Information Assets, having an adverse impact on performance or ability to meet regulatory or legal obligations, or on Community Fibre's reputation or brand.

+-------------------+--------------------------------------------------+ | > Category | | +:=================:+==================================================+ | | - Unauthorised access to premises | | | | | | - Unauthorised access to systems or applications | | | i.e. externally by hacking or internally | | | through circumvention of access privileges | | | | | | - Loss or theft of computer equipment and/or | | | sensitive information | | | | | | - User ID and/or password compromise | | | | | | - Misdirection of sensitive mail / fax / email | | | | | | - Accidental broadcast of sensitive email | | | | | | - Theft or deliberate leaks of information | +-------------------+--------------------------------------------------+ | | - Data input, operator or program error | | | | | | - Virus or malicious code | | | | | | - Hacking - unauthorised use of systems, | | | applications or hacking tools | | | | | | - Inappropriate use of corporate resources, such | | | as the internet | | | | | | - Fraudulent activities - unauthorised | | | manipulation of data | | | | | | - Absence of, or poor, change control | +-------------------+--------------------------------------------------+ | | - Fire, flood or power failure | | | | | | - Hardware/software/communications failure | | | | | | - Failure of environmental controls | | | | | | - Sabotage or vandalism | | | | | | - Loss or failure of backup media | | | | | | - Equipment theft | | | | | | - Force majeure | +-------------------+--------------------------------------------------+

Some Incidents are normal day-to-day activities such as the resetting of a password, or a printing error. These do not qualify as Information Security Incidents, and such cases need to be logged with the IT Helpdesk in the regular manner.

An Information Security Incident or Weakness may be identified by any employee. All suspected or detected breaches of security must be reported to an appropriate contact as soon as possible after identification. Information Security Incidents can be divided into three categories: IT Incidents, Business or Network Incidents.

docs.title: IT Incidents
docs.text:
This will include (but will not be limited to):

  • Breaches of the Community Fibre Access Control Policy or any of the sub policies (i.e., Privileged Access Rights Policy).

  • Inappropriate use of IT Assets including harassment or illegal material.

  • Malicious code attacks e.g. viruses, worms, etc.

  • Hoaxes

  • Unauthorised access to Community Fibre information.

  • Network attacks or Denial of Service Attacks (DoS).

  • Suspected probing or scanning of the network.

  • Telephone system failure.

  • Compromise of information or asset integrity.

  • Any alerts / suspicious activity on security critical systems, internal systems, or applications and application platforms that prove to be a real security alert.

  • Any illegal activity.

  • The potential for any of the above to occur.

docs.title: Business Incidents
docs.text:
This will include (but will not be limited to):

  • Breaches of the Community Fibre Acceptable Usage Policy e.g. email / web abuse.

  • Power outages

  • Harm to an individual because of the compromise of Community Fibre Information Asset.

  • Damage or disaster.

  • Theft and loss of IT hardware and software applications.

  • The theft or loss of Community Fibre information (including documents and files).

  • Racist, sexist or other material which seeks to denigrate any class of individuals.

  • Defamatory or other illegal material.

  • The loss of a Community Fibre site, at which processing, and storage of Community Fibre information takes place, for more than one working day.

  • The likelihood that Community Fibre will be brought into disrepute or might suffer reputational damage.

  • A significant impact on the ability of Community Fibre to perform its duties.

  • An event that is of interest to local or national press.

  • The potential for any of the above to occur.

docs.title: Network Incidents
docs.text:
This will include (but will not be limited to):

  • Breaches of the Community Fibre Access Control Policy or any of the sub policies (i.e., Privileged Access Rights Policy).

  • Deviation from the Physical Security Standard.

  • Routing anomalies, such as BGP route leaks, unauthorised prefix announcements.

  • Network attacks or Denial of Service Attacks (DoS)

  • Failures in customer network provisioning, such as misconfiguration of ONTs or CPEs leading to service degradation or outages.

  • Congestion or capacity issues in core network segments, such as overloaded aggregation switches, transit links, or peering exchanges.

  • Security vulnerabilities in network protocols, including exploits targeting core elements like DNS or DHCP servers.

  • Physical tampering or unauthorised access to network infrastructure, such as at street cabinets, data centres, or customer installation points.

  • Environmental impacts on network assets, including flooding, overheating, or electromagnetic interference affecting core fibre runs or customer modems.

  • Integration failures with third-party networks, such as issues at internet exchange points or upstream provider interconnects.

  • Monitoring and alerting system failures specific to networks.

  • Compliance-related network events, such as failures to enforce traffic shaping under net neutrality rules or data retention obligations for customer sessions.

  • SLA violations due to core or customer network performance issues.

  • Regulatory non-compliance incidents, such as failures to report data breaches involving customer network data under UK GDPR or TSA/Ofcom guidelines.

  • The potential for any of the above to occur.

docs.title: Incident Detection and Reporting
docs.text:
When first detecting or suspecting an Incident or security weakness, you must follow these steps:

  • Ensure that immediate actions are taken to safeguard peoples' Health & Safety.

  • Immediately stop working on any affected IT asset.

  • Without delay, report the Incident to an appropriate point of contact.

  • If you feel that impact of the Incident is, or might become significant, ensure you report this directly to a contact. Do not send an e-mail or leave a message.

  • Follow the instructions of the person to whom you report the Incident, and any further instructions that are given by those who are managing resolution of the Incident.

  • Do not tell anyone else about the Incident, unless they have a justifiable need to know, or if you are following specific instructions from a manager or the Incident Reporting Contact.

docs.title: Reporting IT Incidents
docs.text:
When reporting an IT Incident, in addition to the above, ensure you have the following information available to support prompt investigation.

  • Your contact details.

  • Your location.

  • ID of the affected Asset(s) (if known).

  • What the symptoms are; i.e. what makes you think this is an Incident;

  • What actions you have taken so far.

  • Any information as to what could have triggered the Incident.

  • Any symptoms of the problem or any messages appearing on the screen.

docs.title: Prohibited Actions -- IT incidents
docs.text:
• If an Incident occurs, do not attempt any of the following.

  • Do not try to investigate an Incident yourself.

  • Do not try to prove a suspected weakness -- testing weaknesses might be interpreted as a potential misuse of the system.

  • Do not try to shut down an infected machine but wait until you receive advice from IT staff.

  • Do not try to have "a quick look" as this can invalidate evidence.

  • Do not forward any emails containing a suspected virus or malicious software.

  • Do not copy or forward any material that could be considered offensive or obscene.

  • Do not try to remove any suspect software. This must only be done by IT staff.

  • Do not transfer any files or removable IT assets to other computers.

  • Do not tell anyone outside Community Fibre of the Incident, all client / media contact must be referred to the dedicated point of contact.

docs.title: Information Security Officer
docs.text:
The Information Security Officer (Head of Security) is responsible for:

  • Reviewing and filing logs for all Information Security Incidents that occur, thus acting as the 'incident scribe'.

  • Completing and then maintaining the associated Incident Response report.

  • Presenting a summary of all reported Incidents and actions taken at each ISMS Board meeting.

  • Conducting analysis (or provide information required) of Incidents, to identify trends and notable lessons learned from successes and failures, and report these to the ISMS Board (not less than annually).

  • Analysing available external threat/vulnerability/Incident information to identify trends and notable lessons from both successes and failures and report findings to the ISMS Board (not less than annually).

docs.title: Information Security Management Board
docs.text:
The Information Security Management Forum is responsible for:

  • Presenting a summary of all reported Incidents at each ISMS Board meeting.

  • Determining if any remediation actions have resolved the Incident to a satisfactory conclusion.

  • Receiving periodic analysis reports from the Information Security Officer and determining if existing controls are sufficient, to protect the organisation against identified or emergent threats or vulnerabilities.

  • Consider Incidents and any identified Weaknesses against the Risk Assessment and Treatment Plan.

docs.title: Detecting a Compromise
docs.text:
The following is a small subset of the possible security events that would require investigation:

  • Malware detection

  • File integrity monitor alert

  • Log monitor alert

  • Unknown or unexpected outgoing Internet network traffic from data processing environments

  • Presence of unexpected IP addresses or routing

  • Unknown or unexpected network traffic

  • Unknown or unexpected services and applications configured to launch automatically on system boot

  • Unknown files, software and devices installed on systems

  • Unexplained modification or deletion of data

  • Anti-virus programs malfunctioning or becoming disabled for unknown reasons

  • Excessive failed login attempts in system authentication and event logs

  • Vendor or third-party connections made to any CFL environment without prior consent and/or a ticket

  • SQL Injection attempts or strange code in web server logs

  • Authentication event log modifications (i.e., unexplained event logs are being deleted)

  • Suspicious after-hours file system activity

  • Systems rebooting or shutting down for unknown reasons

  • Unexpected file lengths, sizes or dates, especially for system files

  • Unexplained new user accounts

  • Presence of archived/compressed or unknown encrypted files in system directories

  • Variances in log chronology or timestamps

docs.title: Assigning a category and severity
docs.text:
The generation of 1 or more Information Security Events needs to be assigned a Severity with an associated Scope, before the correct resources that are required to mitigate the incident can be allocated in a timely manner.

The Scope can be of any scale e.g., from a single laptop, a site, a data centre, the head-office and may well change during the incident. The Severity assignment is dependent on the prevailing Scope. For example, the resources allocated to a malware hit on a single laptop might be limited to disabling its access (with subsequent handling within the Service Desk). At the other end of the scale the infection of an entire site forming a botnet would all but instantaneously be allocated the maximum available resources.

docs.title: Triage
docs.text:
Confirmed or even suspected loss or theft of any material must be immediately investigated so that 'Containment and Exposure limitation' is the order of the day.

Members of the IT Operations and Security Operations team act on alerts collated via the systems detailed within [1]. Security Operations team will work closely with colleagues in the Technology, Network Technology or Operations teams. It may be the case that a true security incident is rapidly escalated to where contacts need to be made external and potentially to the company.

All actions are priority based dependent on the assigned severity [1]. It should be kept in mind that a full scale (e.g., denial of service) attack on 1 company target may be used to obscure a low-grade attack on another target. The central monitoring platform must be kept under constant review to separate out the actual targets that are under attack at any given point in time.

  • Breaches relating to customer data or other data protection issues may well need to be reported in a short timescale.

  • Significant outages or incidents of network infrastructure may well need to be reported to Ofcom in a short timescale.

  • Wherever there is any suspicion of criminal activity then the Incident Response Team must rapidly decide as to whether forensics specialists are to be called in, though the affected systems can be isolated.

The preservation of evidence:

  1. Do not access or alter compromised systems (i.e., do not log on at all to the machine and change passwords, do not log in as root or Administrator).

  2. Do not turn the compromised machine off. Instead, isolate compromised systems from the network (i.e., unplug cable).

  3. Preserve logs and electronic evidence, ensuring that records are complete, unaltered, and collected in a form admissible for legal or disciplinary proceedings (e.g., maintain chain of custody documentation).

  4. Log all actions taken, including timestamps, personnel involved, and verification that collection systems were operational and functioning correctly.

  5. Be on 'high' alert and monitor all critical business systems with customer and other critical data.

  6. Ensure evidence is identified, collected, acquired, and preserved by qualified and certified personnel who are legally entitled to handle digital evidence, without making assumptions about its future relevance in litigation.

  7. Where applicable, create electronic replicas that are identical to physical evidence counterparts.

  8. Seek legal advice or involve law enforcement authorities as soon as possible to prevent accidental or intentional destruction of evidence and to align with regulatory, contractual, and jurisdictional requirements

  9. Specifically for cases of suspected fraud then the CFO must be contacted.

  10. The Media representative may well need to be brought in for cases that affect customer data and Community Fibre's corporate profile.

  11. Technology or Network Technology or Operations team members may be called upon to isolate systems and recover them from back-up or create further virtual machines if the original ones are under forensic analysis.

docs.title: Lessons Learned
docs.text:
All completed security incident analysis reports are completed by the ISO (Head of Security) and stored and maintained by the ISO (OneDrive) and may include:

  • Associated documented processes require updating and propagation.

  • New hardware or software defenses need to investigate as a priority.

  • Further formal training is required.

  • Disciplinary action must be taken.

  • Whether third party analysis and associated penetration testing is required to provide assurance that the incident has been successfully resolved.

  • All security incidents would be raised in the next bi-weekly Security Operations stand-up; or an out-of-cycle meeting may be called for serious incidents.

  • Ongoing trends analysis is essential to ensure that lessons can be learned over time so that resources can be appropriately focused.

docs.title: Incident Response Improvements
docs.text: The Incident Response Processes can be tested as part of business continuity planning and in any event on an ongoing ad-hoc basis as part of normal operations. Post-incident reviews must be conducted. This review will identify lessons learned, assess the effectiveness of the response, and evaluate any gaps or improvements needed. The outcomes of the review will be considered at an appropriate governance level (e.g., by the nominated board-level person or committee responsible for security oversight) and used to inform and update the incident response policy, procedures, and processes as necessary to enhance future preparedness and resilience.

docs.title: Legal Requirements
docs.text: The Technology department must call on legal expertise at the earliest indication that a breach of criminal or civil legislation is underway or indeed has occurred, to determine the correct course of action. That said all personnel must also have a base understanding e.g., in terms of the preservation of forensic evidence so that any subsequent judicial proceedings are not prejudiced.

docs.title: Data Protection
docs.text:
The 6^th^ principle of the DPA (see reference [5]) states:

Personal data shall be processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security of the personal data, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measures ('integrity and confidentiality')."

docs.title: When to report?
docs.text: +----------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Reference [6] states: When a | | personal data breach has occurred, you need to establish the | | likelihood of the risk to people's rights and freedoms. If a risk is | | likely, you must notify the ICO; if a risk is unlikely, you don't | | have to report it. However, if you decide you don't need to report | | the breach, you need to be able to justify this decision, so you | | should document it. | | | | - The UK GDPR introduces a duty on all organisations to report | | certain personal data breaches to the relevant supervisory | | authority. You must do this within 72 hours of becoming aware of | | the breach, where feasible. | | | | - If the breach is likely to result in a high risk of adversely | | affecting individuals' rights and freedoms, you must also inform | | those individuals without undue delay. | | | | - You should ensure you have robust breach detection, investigation | | and internal reporting procedures in place. This will facilitate | | decision-making about whether you need to notify the relevant | | supervisory authority or the affected individuals, or both. | | | | - You must also keep a record of any personal data breaches, | | regardless of whether you are required to notify. | | | | If a breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and | | freedoms of individuals, the UK GDPR says you must inform those | | concerned directly and without undue delay. In other words, this | | should take place as soon as possible. | | | | A 'high risk' means the requirement to inform individuals is higher | | than for notifying the ICO. Again, you will need to assess both the | | severity of the potential or actual impact on individuals because of | | a breach and the likelihood of this occurring. If the impact of the | | breach is more severe, the risk is higher; if the likelihood of the | | consequences is greater, then again, the risk is higher. In such | | cases, you will need to promptly inform those affected, particularly | | if there is a need to mitigate an immediate risk of damage to them. | | One of the main reasons for informing individuals is to help them | | take steps to protect themselves from the effect of a breach. | +======================================================================+

docs.text: Reference [6] states that the data security breach reporting form should be submitted.

docs.title: Where to report?
docs.text:
• casework@ico.gsi.gov.uk

  • Wycliffe House, Water Lane, Wilmslow, Cheshire SK9 5AF

**

  1. The Computer Misuse Act

References [8] and [9] detail the following crimes that should be reported to the local constabulary or SOCA as relevant:

  1. Unauthorised access to computer material.

  2. Unauthorised access with intent to commit or facilitate a crime.

  3. Unauthorised modification of computer material.

  4. Making, supplying or obtaining anything which can be used in computer misuse offences.

Report to Action Fraud at https://www.actionfraud.police.uk/ or by calling 0300 123 2040. For serious or organised crime, contact the NCA at https://www.nationalcrimeagency.gov.uk/.

  1. Telecommunications Security Framework

Under the Telecommunications (Security) Act 2021, which amends the Communications Act 2003, and in alignment with The Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022 and the associated Telecommunications Security Code of Practice, providers of public electronic communications networks or services have duties to report security compromises. Section 105I of the Communications Act 2003 requires providers to inform Ofcom as soon as reasonably practicable of any security compromise that has a significant impact on the network or service, including:

  • Network or service outages affecting availability, performance, or functionality (resilience incidents).

  • Cyber-security incidents.

  • Pre-positioning attacks (e.g., preparatory actions by threat actors that could lead to future compromises).

A security compromise is considered significant if it has a material impact on the operation of the network or service, such as widespread outages, exposure of sensitive data, or risks to national security.

Section 105J requires providers to inform affected users without undue delay if the compromise is likely to adversely affect them, to enable them to take protective steps. Section 105K requires providers to take specified measures in response to a security compromise to remedy or mitigate its effects.

Providers must also maintain records of all security compromises and cooperate with other providers under Regulation 15 of the 2022 Regulations if a compromise may cause a connected security compromise in another network or service.

Refer to Ofcom\'s guidance for details on significance thresholds and reporting formats. Reports should be submitted to the Ofcom Network Security team via the secure portal or email at network.security@ofcom.org.uk. For further information, see https://www.ofcom.org.uk/internet-based-services/network-security/guidance-for-operators.

docs.title: General Obligations
docs.text:
1. Reference in this Standard to 'include(s)', 'including' or 'in particular' are deemed to have the words \"without limitation\" following them.

  2. Any reference to a directive, statute, statutory provision or subordinate legislation shall (except where the context otherwise requires) be construed as referring to such legislation as amended and in force from time- to-time and to any legislation which re-enacts or consolidates (with or without modification) any such legislation.

  3. Any reference preceded by 'M.x' is a reference to the Telecommunications Security Code of Practice.

  4. This Standard should be read in conjunction with the Telecommunications Security Code of Practice, as published on the GOV.UK website and applicable to all UK Tier 1 and Tier 2 public telecoms providers.

  5. The following table explains the applicability of the appendices to this standard:

Service Appendix

Where the Supplier has been authorised by Comply with Appendix A Community Fibre to store, process, or transmit any Customer Personal Data or any other data classified as Strictly Confidential by Community Fibre

Where the Supplier has been authorised by Comply with Appendix B Community Fibre to store, process, or transmit cardholder Data

Where the Supplier is delivering Contact Comply with the Centre Services requirements of Appendix C

Where the service(s) provided relate to Comply with the the provision of a Cloud solution for use requirements of Appendix D by Community Fibre employees or Supplier staff

All Suppliers Comply with the requirements of Appendix E and Appendix F

Where the Supplier will provide hardware, Comply with Appendix G software, or third-party administration; or Services for Community Fibre's Critical National Infrastructure and thus be within the scope of the Telecommunications Security Act 2021

  1. The Supplier will, in accordance with Good Industry Practice:

a) have in place (and regularly and thoroughly test at its own cost and expense), security arrangements to:

i. protect the access, availability, integrity and confidentiality of Community Fibre Data and any other information relating to Community Fibre and any of its officers, agents, professional advisers, employees, or subcontractors which is disclosed to, or processed or otherwise handled by, the Supplier, any of its personnel or subcontractors; and

ii. ensure that such information is not:

A. other than in accordance with the Supplier Contract or this Standard, destroyed (including deletion); altered (including corruption); or

B. lost, accessed by unauthorised personnel, transferred, or (without appropriate authorisation) disclosed while it is in the possession or under the control of the Supplier or any of the Supplier Personnel.

b) comply with this Standard and any additional policies and standards as agreed with Community Fibre to be applicable to the access and use of Community Fibre Data.

c) maintain security control over its technology and physical storage infrastructure (by using tools that include firewalls, encryption, authentication Services and swipe access);

d) ensure that:

i. all Community Fibre Data is logically segregated and where appropriate, physically segregated, in a separate area from all non-Community Fibre Data and information held by the Supplier, either for itself or on behalf of its other customers or suppliers;

ii. the latest copies of its relevant information security and privacy policies and any other information security standards, procedures, documented requirements and any supporting evidence demonstrating the operation of such policies, standards, procedures and requirements are made available to Community Fibre, free of charge, at Community Fibre's reasonable request;

e) notify Community Fibre of any material changes to the Supplier's information security policies, standards, procedures and documented requirements and provide copies of the same free of charge, at Community Fibre's reasonable request; and

f) detect, respond and recover Services and Community Fibre Data as the result of a security incident occurring, including reporting it to Community Fibre as described in section 8 of this Standard.

1.  In relation to this Standard:

a) Community Fibre will be entitled, upon giving notice to the Supplier, to carry out or engage an independent organisation of its choice to carry out, security audits and tests as it may deem necessary in relation to the Supplier's compliance with its obligations under this Standard, Good Industry Practice, or as a result of an investigation; and

b) the Supplier will co-operate and facilitate any such audit required by Community Fibre of the Supplier's security measures as they apply to the Services.

1.  Where any audit or test reveals any actual or potential security
    or control failure or weakness, the Supplier will promptly, and
    no later than one month after being informed of identified
    risks, notify Community Fibre of any plans to remediate its
    security controls in order to correct such failure or weakness.

2.  Where such changes to the security controls are to address
    non-compliance with the Supplier's security obligations under
    this Standard, such changes will be at no additional cost to
    Community Fibre.

3.  The Supplier must notify Community Fibre when:

a) it is acquired by another company, or when it acquires or merges with another company;

b) any changes to the production of Hardware or Software supplied to Community Fibre occur or are planned which will or may result in such Hardware or Software being produced in a different country or region; or

c) any changes to the services being delivered will or may result in Community Fibre or customer Data being transferred to, accessed from or processed in a different country or region.

1.  This Standard will be reviewed on an annual basis, or as
    required, to ensure it reflects current Community Fibre working
    practices, industry standards and legislative developments.

docs.title: Organisation Security
docs.text:
1. The Supplier will:

a) maintain full compliance with:

i. a recognized information security management standard for the scope of the Services provided to Community Fibre and, where appropriate, will provide relevant documentation and confirm the scope of the services covered by their certification at Community Fibre's request.

ii. NICC ND 1643 where the Services involve interconnecting with the Community Fibre network.

iii. Good Industry Practice.

b) establish any critical functions and dependencies for the delivery of Services and communicate these to Community Fibre in the format of supplied documentation ahead of delivery commencing.

c) document the flows of data involved in the service to be delivered to Community Fibre including the type and criticality of data moving between internal system components and from internal to external system components and share this documentation at request.

d) ensure that:

i. all information security responsibilities are defined, allocated and documented within their organisation; (ii) appropriate information security training and awareness is conducted for all personnel (permanent, contractors and agency) upon hire, following a security incident and annually thereafter;

ii. it has an information security policy in place which is reviewed annually and communicated to all personnel (permanent, contractors and agency) who read and agree to it;

iii. it has an up-to-date privacy policy detailing its handling and classification of data which is reviewed annually and communicated to all personnel (permanent, contractors and agency) who read and agree to it; and

iv. its legal and regulatory requirements are understood and managed.

e) on request, require personnel with access to any Community Fibre Data, Community Fibre Systems or Community Fibre premises to complete Community Fibre's own information security training.

f) support Community Fibre with the monitoring and performance of the security requirements set out in this document.

g) keep all records relating to compliance with the security requirements for at least one year after expiry or earlier termination of the Supplier Contract.

h) conduct appropriate security pre-employment screening and background checks for all personnel (including for example, right to work, employee references, criminal records, financial); and

i) regularly repeat background checks for contractors and personnel who represent a very high risk of security breach or fraud.

1.  Community Fibre will also assess any potential detriment to
    security of the Community Fibre Network. Community Fibre expects
    the Supplier to be transparent and open about their security
    practices and to support responsible, independent security
    researchers. For example, through engagement such as responding
    to, triaging and investigating responsibly disclosed issues.
    (TSA)

docs.title: Risk Management
docs.text:
1. The Supplier acknowledges Community Fibre must take appropriate measures to identify and reduce risk of security compromise:

a) during the formation, existence or termination of a contract with the Supplier; (M4.01) and

b) that may arise from any other contract for the supply, provision or making available of any hardware or software, services or facilities in connection with the provision of a service, including public electronic communications network / service. (M4.01)

1.  The Supplier must have formally documented information security
    risk assessment and management processes and procedures in
    place, which are appropriate and demonstrably followed, for the
    identification, recording, mitigation and management of security
    risks to Community Fibre Data.

2.  In relation to the Services, the Supplier will, with agreement
    from Community Fibre, identify any subcontractor that is
    critical to provide the Services, or which has access to
    Community Fibre Data, and ensure that they comply with the
    requirements of this Standard or requirements not less stringent
    than this.

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text:
1. Where a Supplier is given access to the Community Fibre Network via accounts created by Community Fibre:

a) These must have access restricted to the Data, applications and System(s) that are required to be accessed; and

b) the Supplier must follow Community Fibre 'joiner, mover and leaver' processes in relation to them.

1.  Where, access to any Community Fibre System is given to Supplier
    Personnel via accounts controlled by the Supplier, in relation
    to access control the Supplier will as a minimum:

a) ensure that a robust documented process for managing joiners, movers and leavers in a timely manner is implemented, including provision for the removal of unexpected leavers through an emergency procedure.

b) only permit access to specific individual Supplier Personnel who have a clearly defined requirement for access, and not to groups of individuals.

c) grant, monitor and revoke privileges only through a clear chain authority and in a timely manner.

d) ensure that:

i. access to any system source code is restricted to only those required to have access; and

ii. allocation and use of privileged access rights are restricted and controlled.

e) conduct a review of logical access control every six months to ensure that all staff have the correct access for their current role; and

f) review privileged access on not less than a quarterly basis.

1.  On all Supplier Systems which store, process or have the
    capability to access Community Fibre Data, in relation to access
    control, the Supplier will:

a) immediately disable or delete the User IDs of those individuals who are no longer authorised to access any Community Fibre System;

b) ensure that Community Fibre Data is at all times protected by System access controls to ensure that it is not accessed, modified, or deleted by unauthorised personnel;

c) ensure that all Supplier Personnel have unique User IDs allocated to them; and

d) establish password control Systems that ensure that passwords allocated conform to standards in accordance with Good Industry Practice and are not able to be used by unauthorised parties.

1.  The Supplier will ensure that physical access to Community Fibre
    assets held by the Supplier is managed and protected
    appropriately, including:

a) IT systems processing or storing Community Fibre Data to be located in an area which can only be accessed by authorised Supplier Personnel.

b) laptops and other computers issued by Community Fibre to be kept secure by the individual to whom they are issued, and returned to Community Fibre when no longer required; and

c) any removable media containing Community Fibre Data to be encrypted and kept locked when not in use.

docs.title: Data Security
docs.text:
1. The Supplier will:

a) ensure:

i. that in relation to Community Fibre Data appropriate technical and organisational measures are taken against unauthorised or unlawful processing, accidental damage, or destruction loss.

ii. all Community Fibre Data in transit and at rest is always protected using appropriate technical and operational controls.

b) arrange for penetration testing - by a suitably qualified person -- of any Internet facing service that could allow access to Community Fibre Data, before deployment and after any significant change.

c) Ensure that any assets that hold, store, or process any Community Fibre Data including physical devices, Software applications, information assets and external information Systems are:

i. built to a defined template through cloning, use of a 'gold build', or automated deployment;

ii. recorded on an asset register which is regularly updated and maintained; and

iii. managed to ensure minimum information security standards are met.

d) afford the same level of protection for printed output e.g., Customer Personal Data, reports, listings, mailings, bank, and financial details etc. as for other forms of Data i.e., restrict access, control copying and store securely.

e) in relation to back-up and storage of Community Fibre Data:

i. ensure that Supplier Systems and Software are backed up so that prompt recovery can take place in times of failure;

ii. regularly make back-up copies of Community Fibre Data and Software in accordance with Good Industry Practice and as agreed with Community Fibre, and keep such backup copies secure;

iii. document the method and location of back-ups, the type of back-ups and the volume of Community Fibre Data that is being backed-up and the reasons why that Data is being retained, in line with Good Industry Practice and any Community Fibre requirements for data retention; and

iv. ensure that Community Fibre Data is not, and cannot be, stored on any personal devices used by Supplier Personnel.

f) in relation to security and handling of media containing Community Fibre data, when under the Supplier's control:

i. control and physically protect computer media (whether fixed or removable);

ii. establish documented procedures for handling Community Fibre Data; and

iii. control, store and dispose of computer media handled by a subcontractor in line with written procedures agreed with Community Fibre.

g. within an agreed timeframe, securely dispose of all Community Fibre Data held by the Supplier when no longer required, using formal procedures which include:

i. a process to identify the items that might require secure disposal;

ii. destruction of physical media and assets in line with current industry standards and no less stringent than those set out in Appendix F;

iii. sanitisation of any re-usable media such that Community Fibre Data is made unrecoverable;

iv. logging disposal of assets in order to maintain an audit trail including evidence of that disposal through holding certificates of destruction for at least 12 months after destruction;

v. returning any assets owned by Community Fibre; and

vi. securely deleting or destroying back-up Community Fibre Data held on the written instruction of Community Fibre, save where the Supplier can demonstrate to Community Fibre's satisfaction that the Supplier is unable to do so due to a legal obligation or where required by any regulator acting within the scope of its authority.

1.  If the Supplier has any doubts about their part in ensuring the
    continued security of Community Fibre's operations, then this
    must be raised immediately with their contact at Community
    Fibre. In particular, the Supplier must:

a) be aware of Community Fibre's security needs which are relevant to them, and which are detailed in the contracts and in this Standard (M10.02); and

b) understands their role where responsibilities are shared between Community Fibre and them and maintain documentation of such. (M10.03)

1.  If Supplier intends to process, or permit the processing of,
    personal data provided by, or on behalf of Community Fibre,
    because of, or in connection with, the Supplier Contract,
    outside of the United Kingdom, Supplier may only do so:

a) following Community Fibre's written agreement;

b) following the undertaking of a TIA by Community Fibre, which Supplier shall contribute to, if requested; and

c) in accordance with this Standard, the Supplier Contract and any relevant ancillary agreements e.g., a data processing agreement or data sharing agreement.

1.  If Supplier intends to use a machine learning or artificial
    intelligence ("AI") solution for processing Community Fibre
    Data, including for training the Supplier's own models, then
    this may only be done:

a) with specific permission from Community Fibre.

b) if the data will be contained within a closed model / not publicly available; and

c) with assurance that data is not used to train other models.

docs.title: Protective Technology
docs.text:
1. If the Supplier controls the administration and operation of any specific environments and networks required for the performance of the Services and processing of any Community Fibre Data, including any Third-Party Services managed by the Supplier, it will:

a) in relation to cryptography:

i. only send Community Fibre Data via communications networks external to the Community Fibre network in an encrypted form;

ii. store Community Fibre Data in an encrypted form when at rest;

iii. ensure that, when cryptography is used, only current industry standard algorithms are used and, products which have received appropriate accreditations in accordance with Good Industry Practice;

iv. strictly limit access to cryptographic keys to those who have a need to know, and ensure that any master keys cannot be accessed by any one individual;

v. ensure that the information protected by encryption is transmitted over a different communication channel than the keys used to govern the cryptographic process, or use a standard and approved key exchange protocol;

vi. ensure that cryptographic keys and related keying materials used in the process are not stored anywhere in unencrypted form; and

vii. ensure that whenever cryptography is used, the sole readable version of Community Fibre Data is not deleted until receipt and decryption of the encrypted file has been confirmed.

b) in relation to protection from malicious Software:

i. implement controls to prevent and detect the introduction of malicious Software and viruses into any Systems holding Community Fibre Data or used by Community Fibre or the Supplier in relation to the Services; and

ii. implement commercial grade anti-virus software and ensure it is kept up to date.

c) in relation to network security controls:

i. establish appropriate controls to ensure the security of Community Fibre Data in networks, and the protection of connected Services from unauthorised access;

ii. implement controls to safeguard the integrity and confidentiality of Community Fibre Data passing over public networks, and to protect the connected Systems;

iii. implement controls to protect against data leakage;

iv. authenticate connections to remote computer Systems; and

v. configure firewalls and gateway devices to allow only authorised traffic to flow through them.

d) in relation to development processes:

i. carry out Software/application development and testing with Community Fibre test Data or anonymised production Community Fibre Data where that test data has been anonymised or pseudonymised to the extent that it is considered so under the terms of the relevant Data Protection Laws to ensure it cannot be traced back to a living individual, unless otherwise agreed in writing by Community Fibre;

ii. ensure separate transactions are used for testing or training purposes from transactions used for production processing;

iii. where Systems are operated by the Supplier, ensure that access to compilers, assemblers, editors, and other general-purpose utilities within the test environment is restricted; and

iv. provide assurances/warranties that none of the Software contains undocumented features or hidden mechanisms that could be used to compromise the Software\'s security.

e) in relation to Software developed specifically for Community Fibre, the Supplier must ensure:

i. the Software provider adheres to secure code production guidelines, which must include code inspection to verify the absence of security weaknesses;

ii. for "off-the shelf" Software, the Supplier must satisfy itself that any Software licence adequately describes the Software capabilities, which must be validated by the Supplier's own security testing at the Supplier's own cost;

iii. to obtain written confirmation from any third-party providing Software in relation to the Services that the Software will not require the modification or renewal of existing Community Fibre computer security Systems; and

iv. to not utilise any free or downloaded code not controlled by the Supplier (e.g., shared code-banks, repositories from on-line sources that may harbour unknown procedures, malware, or access rights).

docs.title: Security Monitoring
docs.text:
1. If requested by Community Fibre in relation to the Services provided, the Supplier will provide assurance that newly identified vulnerabilities are mitigated within defined timescales no longer than those outlined in Appendix E. Compliance must be demonstrated using supporting evidence at Community Fibre's request.

    2. All assets processing Community Fibre Data must be monitored regularly to identify security events/ incidents and verify the effectiveness of protective measures.

    3. In relation to Community Fibre Data, all system, application, and user access must be logged and monitored, and logs must be:

a) stored centrally, away from source and protected from unauthorised access, where central storage of logs is not possible, logs must be securely stored locally;

b) maintained with sufficient quality to be used as admissible evidence during forensic investigation;

c) reviewed regularly to ensure the admissibility of evidence as part of any forensic investigations; and

1.  protected against tampering and unauthorised access. The
    supplier must ensure that appropriate technical controls are in
    place to prevent the accidental or malicious exfiltration of
    Community Fibre Data via external electronic communication
    channels such as USB mass storage devices, email, and web-based
    file transfer sites e.g., Data Loss Prevention, Web filtering
    and email filtering.

docs.title: Incident Management
docs.text:
1. The Supplier will ensure that Supplier Personnel are aware of their roles in identifying, reporting, and responding to information security events or incidents.

  2. If the Supplier becomes aware of any actual, potential, or attempted Breach of Security; or any breach of its obligations under this Third-Party Security Standard, it will immediately:

a) notify Community Fibre incident management team and the relevant business partner at Community Fibre of the actual or suspected breaches of security of its obligations under this Third-Party Security Standard and report on the potential effect of such breach to Community Fibre as soon as possible (and, in any event, within 24 hours);

b) identify a single point of contact for Community Fibre to liaise with during the management of the security incident;

c) take immediate steps to contain any breach to prevent further impact as appropriate;

d) take all reasonable steps necessary, as approved by Community Fibre, to remedy such breach (to the extent that it is capable of remediation) or protect Community Fibre Data against any such potential or attempted breach or threat, promptly investigate such breach and provide Community Fibre with regular updates throughout;

e) advise Community Fibre of any Supplier Personnel implicated in the incident and take appropriate disciplinary action, including suspension if required, upon Community Fibre's request;

f) promptly take measures to ensure that such breach does not occur again and provide a written report to Community Fibre detailing the measures taken;

g) document the response to the matter and finding of the investigation into such breach and issue this to Community Fibre as soon as practical whilst continuing to provide investigation and remediation action point updates to Community Fibre, until such time they are completed to the satisfaction of Community Fibre;

h) where criminal activity is suspected, or a breach of contractual or regulatory requirements and, if requested by Community Fibre:

i. engage an independent third-party approved by Community Fibre to gather legally admissible evidence or contact the law enforcement agencies;

ii. allow Community Fibre access to conduct its own investigations or work with the engaged third-party; and

iii. ensure all communications with third parties or the media are agreed in writing by Community Fibre before release.

 1.  Any costs that Community Fibre incurs that are associated with
     any Breach of Security response or investigation will be
     charged back to the Supplier, including audit costs and
     expenses.

docs.title: Business Continuity
docs.text:
1. In relation to the Services, the Supplier will:

a) establish resilience requirements to support delivery of critical Services to Community Fibre; and

b) ensure adequate capacity to maintain availability.

1.  In relation to the Services provided to Community Fibre, the
    Supplier will ensure:

a) response plans (incident response, business continuity, incident recovery and disaster recovery) are in place and tested annually; and

b) the response, continuity and recovery plans are executed during and after an event.

1.  The Supplier will ensure that the Systems required to provide
    Services to Community Fibre continue to operate in pre-defined
    function states to achieve availability (e.g., normal
    operations, during recovery, under duress).

2.  In relation to the location of computers and facilities used to
    store Community Fibre Data, the Supplier will ensure that they
    are able to continue operations despite disruption to:

a) power supply;

b) telecommunications links; and

c) environmental controls.

1.  If requested by Community Fibre, the Supplier will, in relation
    to Community Fibre Data and the Services, provide evidence of
    the plans in place and that they are regularly tested.

2.  If applicable, the Supplier will ensure that relevant response
    and recovery planning and testing are conducted with critical
    Suppliers/providers.

docs.title: Cloud Security
docs.text:
1. Where the service or services to be provided relate to the provision of a Cloud Service including SaaS, IaaS, PaaS, FaaS solutions, there must be a Community Fibre colleague nominated as the business owner who will be responsible for the procurement, development, operation, maintenance, and eventual termination of the service.

  2. There may be a shared responsibility between the Supplier and Community Fibre around the following:

a) Data Classification and accountability.

b) Client and Endpoint Protection;

c) Identity and Access Management.

d) Host Infrastructure; and

e) Physical Security.

f) Network Controls

1.  Supplier must evidence the effectiveness of applicable security
    controls for which they or a subcontractor have responsibility,
    either through an audit conducted by Community Fibre or by
    evidence of an audit by an independent external auditor - such
    as SOC2 Type II or Cyber Essentials Plus.

docs.title: Appendix A -- Applicable for Personal or Strictly Confidential Data
docs.text:
The following requirements apply if the Supplier has been authorised by Community Fibre to store, process or transmit any Customer Personal Data including sensitive personal data or Special Category Data or any other data classified as Strictly Confidential by Community Fibre. This could include but is not limited to the following types of data:

  • Personal Details - name, date of birth, salary, nationality

  • Account Details - Call line identification, devices ID, IP address, cookies, service history

  • Company Data -- company contact details, county court judgements, bankruptcy information

  • Financial Details -- Bank details, payment account history, historic bills

  • Interaction History -- copies of correspondence, call recordings, chat transcripts, engineer fault notices

docs.title: Organisation
docs.text:
1. The Supplier will document a security management plan which shall contain, as a minimum, an outline of:

a) the assets and information they process and/or access.

b) the results of their risk assessment in relation to these.

c) other security implemented.

d) organisational roles delegated responsibility for these controls and security measures.

e) the controls they have in place to manage the identified risk.

1.  The security management plan will be updated no less than
    annually and provided to Community Fibre on request.

2.  The supplier will provide information security awareness and
    training to supplier staff.

3.  The Supplier must have established priorities for business and
    security objectives.

4.  The Supplier will:

a) ensure that appropriate information security training and awareness is conducted for all Supplier Personnel upon hire and at least annually, which includes content around the handling of Customer Personal Data in line with the appropriate legislation; and

b) nominate a member of its personnel as its security officer to act as a single point of contact for all security related matters between the Supplier and Community Fibre.

docs.title: Risk Management
docs.text:
1. The Supplier must have an established formal risk assessment framework based on Good Industry Practice.

    2. The Supplier will maintain a register of all information security risks related to the service and will notify Community Fibre of any high risk identified which could affect Community Fibre data in a prompt and timely manner along with the proposed remediation plan for that risk.

    3. The Supplier will ensure that its risk management programme includes the supply chain in relation to the Services.

    4. Any areas where the Supplier does not fully meet a requirement of its obligations under this Third-party Security Standard, must immediately be raised as a risk through the risk management processes and escalated to Community Fibre.

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text:
1. On all Supplier Systems which store, process, or have the capability to access Community Fibre Data, the following access controls will be applied:

a) where external access is possible, 2-Factor Authentication (2FA) shall be implemented and utilised;

b) role based access control will be applied with the principle of least privilege being implemented;

c) all access will be logged and monitored; and

d) the Supplier must inform Community Fibre of any personnel who have privileged access to Community Fibre systems when they leave the Supplier.

1.  No generic or shared accounts shall be used to access Supplier
    Systems. Conflicting duties and areas of responsibility shall be
    segregated to reduce unauthorised modification or misuse.

docs.title: Data Security
docs.text:
1. The Supplier shall ensure that any assets identified as holding or processing Community Fibre Data are prioritised based on their classification, criticality, and business value and are formally managed throughout their lifecycle including removal and transfer.

    2. Where the Supplier has direct access into internal Community Fibre Systems holding personal Data:

a) access to:

i. non-Community Fibre approved external email, social media, online storage, and other modes of external electronic communication shall be restricted while processing to reduce the potential for external distribution of such data; and

ii. webmail, social media, and file-sharing sites will be prohibited, unless authorised by Community Fibre and will be blocked using web-filtering controls. Access to gambling and pornographic sites shall be prohibited and will be blocked using web-filtering controls.

docs.title: Protective Technology
docs.text:
1. If the Supplier controls the administration and operation of any specific environments and networks required for the performance of the Services and processing of any Community Fibre Data, including any cloud Services or any Third-Party Services managed by the Supplier, it will:

a) In relation to operational procedures and responsibilities:

i. implement mechanisms and processes in accordance with Good Industry Practice to minimise the risk of negligent or deliberate System misuse;

ii. isolate development and testing facilities from Community Fibre's operational Systems; and

iii. segregate the Systems and network that processes Community Fibre Data, including printing facilities, from the Supplier\'s other networks. The level of segregation will be both physical and logical (or in the case of cloud Services, just logical).

docs.title: Security Monitoring
docs.text:
1. In relation to Community Fibre Data, all system, application and user access logs, the Supplier must ensure that:

a) appropriate privacy and protection controls are in place for any logs that contain personal Data;

b) privileged users shall not have permission that would make it possible to erase or deactivate logs of their own activities;

c) information on which Community Fibre related assets are monitored and their subsequent use cases/monitoring rules can be provided upon request;

d) monitoring rules are regularly reviewed and tuned to reflect false positives/negatives.

1.  Where the supplier has direct access into Community Fibre
    internal systems holding personal data:

a) access to non-Community Fibre approved external email, social media, online storage, and other modes of external electronic communication shall be restricted while processing to reduce the potential for external distribution of such data; and

b) access to webmail, social media, and file-sharing sites will be prohibited, unless authorised by Community Fibre and will be blocked using web-filtering controls. Access to gambling and pornographic sites shall be prohibited and will be blocked using web-filtering controls.

docs.title: Incident Management
docs.text:
1. The Supplier must have established incident management processes and procedures for the Supplier\'s computers and networks used in relation to the Services.

    2. If applicable, during or after a Breach of Security, the Supplier will conduct a full forensic analysis, ensuring throughout the investigation that:

a) the relevant local laws are adhered to; and

b) the chain of custody is maintained.

1.  In the event that the Supplier becomes aware of any actual,
    potential or attempted Breach of Security, it will immediately
    (and, in any event, within 24 hours) notify Community Fibre
    security via email to <security@communityfibre.co.uk>

docs.title: Appendix B -- Applicable for Cardholder Data (PCI)
docs.text:
1. In accordance with paragraph 1.2(e) above, and in addition to Appendix A, if the Supplier has been authorised by Community Fibre to store, process or transmit cardholder Data, the following also applies:

  2. At all times, the Supplier must process all cardholder Data in accordance with Community Fibre\'s processes and in accordance with the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS) and, if applicable, the PCI Payment Application Data Security Standard (PA DSS), including by:

a) installing and maintaining a firewall configuration to protect cardholder Data;

b) encrypting transmission of cardholder Data across open, public networks;

c) not using vendor-supplied defaults for system passwords and other security parameters;

d) regularly updating anti-virus Software or programs;

e) developing and maintaining secure Systems and applications;

f) restricting access to cardholder Data on a business need to know basis;

g) assigning a unique ID to each person with computer access;

h) restricting physical access to cardholder Data;

i) tracking and monitoring all access to network resources and cardholder Data;

j) maintaining a policy that addresses information security for all Supplier Personnel;

k) ensuring shared hosting providers protect the cardholder Data environment; and

l) regularly testing security Systems and processes.

1.  The Supplier must have undergone PCI DSS and, if applicable, the
    PA DSS compliance assessment and must be validated as compliant
    and must provide evidence on an annual basis or upon request
    from Community Fibre. It is the responsibility of the Supplier
    to check for updates to the relevant standards to ensure they
    are understood and implemented.

2.  The Supplier agrees that its use of Customer Personal Data,
    merchant Data and cardholder Data must only be for the purposes
    of assisting the completion of transactions, loyalty programmes,
    fraud control Services or for any other use specifically
    required by law or Community Fibre.

3.  The Supplier will ensure that a PCI representative or any
    approved Third-party nominated by any such PCI representative
    will be provided with full co-operation and access to conduct
    security reviews in the event of any security intrusion,
    investigation, or breach. Any such review will be conducted to
    validate that the Supplier's operational procedures conform to
    PCI DSS for protecting cardholder Data.

4.  In the event of a suspected or confirmed Breach of Security, the
    Supplier must:

a) promptly (and, in any event, within 24 hours) alert Community Fibre by contacting via email on security@communityfibre.co.uk

b) immediately contain and limit exposure and minimise data loss; and determine if a payment forensic officer is required and, if so, the Supplier must ensure that only a PCI SCC listed forensic investigator is engaged to perform the forensic investigation.

docs.title: Appendix C -- Applicable to the Delivery of Contact Centre and Business Process (BPO) Services
docs.text: Where the service or services to be provided relate to the provision of Contact Centre Services or BPO Services that are undertaken at a Third-Party physical location dedicated to Community Fibre, the following additional security requirements will apply:

docs.title: Organisational Security
docs.text:
1. Establish and publish policies, procedures and standards which addresses Contact Centre and BPO security and put into effect the requirements of this schedule and other appropriate good practice where applicable.

  2. Assign and document overall accountability for the security of the Contact Centre, BPO and Community Fibre Data processed within that environment to a suitably senior member of staff with appropriate experience and authority to make decisions to ensure that risk to Community Fibre data is mitigated.

docs.title: Risk Management
docs.text: 1. A security risk assessment of Contact Centre and BPO operations and facilities shall be conducted and repeated on an annual basis or at the point of change of the service provided and the supplier shall ensure that any risks to Community Fibre Data which emerge are treated and monitored on an ongoing basis in accordance with best practice in risk management. The findings will be retained for at least twelve months after closure and be made available to Community Fibre upon request.

docs.title: Staff Training
docs.text:
1. Appropriate training will be given to all staff with access to Community Fibre Data to ensure that:

a) all legal and statutory obligations are understood and complied with along with Community Fibre specified procedures for ensuring compliance including, but not limited to, the Data Protection Laws and the Computer Misuse Act 1990;

b) Community Fibre Data is processed in a secure manner within the contact centre and BPO environment in compliance with this schedule, the general requirements set out in the Third-Party Security Standard other relevant Community Fibre and Contact Centre and BPO policies, procedures, and practices;

c) Contact Centre Operatives know how to identify potentially fraudulent calls, suspicious behaviours and attempted social engineering techniques and how to respond and report such attempts; and

d) All staff processing Community Fibre customer credit and debit card payments do so in a way which maintains Community Fibre's compliance with the requirements of PCI DSS ensuring that no cardholder data is recorded either in writing or on call recording systems.

e) The training delivered will have a test element with a pass mark to ensure that all staff have assimilated the messages delivered sufficiently to process Community Fibre data competently and securely. Where the testing element is failed front line access will be revoked until completed successfully.

f) Such training will be delivered on employment, before access to the Contact Centre and BPO Environment and Community Fibre Data, and annually thereafter.

g) A record of each employee's record of training will be retained for the period of employment of the employee and 12 months thereafter.

docs.title: Human Resource Management
docs.text:
1. All staff with either direct or indirect access to Community Fibre Data should be subject to preemployment background checks and vetting procedures in accordance with best practice to ensure they do not present a risk of fraudulent activity or unauthorised disclosure, amendment, or destruction of such data.

    2. Such checks shall be re-performed, at a frequency to be agreed with Community Fibre, considering the level of risk identified because of initial checks.

    3. A formal disciplinary process shall be established to address breaches of security policy within the call centre and BPO location.

docs.title: Acceptable Use
docs.text:
1. Access to non-Community Fibre approved external email, social media, online storage, and other modes of external electronic communication shall be restricted while processing Community Fibre Data to reduce the potential for external distribution of such data.

    2. Where Community Fibre data is stored and processed outside of Community Fibre's own systems and environment access to webmail, social media, file-sharing sites, gambling sites and pornographic sites will be prohibited, unless authorised by Community Fibre and will be blocked using web-filtering controls.

docs.title: Identification Verification
docs.text:
1. The correct level of identification verification as determined by Community Fibre's Access Control Policy will be performed before disclosing customer data on a call, processing a customer transaction, or amending customer account details.

    2. Where possible advanced identification and verification techniques such as passive voice biometrics, DTMF (Dual Tone Multi Frequency) verification or phone printing shall be used to assure the identity of the caller while reducing security risk.

docs.title: Use of Mobile Devices
docs.text:
1. All mobile devices, except were authorised by Community Fibre, including those capable of capturing Community Fibre Data via photography, audio, or other recording mechanism such as tablets, phones, smart watches, cameras, and Dictaphones will not be taken by contact centre and BPO staff into any environment where Community Fibre customer calls or Community Fibre Data is being processed. They will be stored securely prior to entering the call centre environment to prevent access until staff leave this environment.

    2. Where so authorised, appropriate processes will be in place to ensure that those mobile devices are used in an appropriate manner.

docs.title: Transfer and Recording of Community Fibre Data
docs.text:
1. Community Fibre Data will only be processed for the purpose or purposes of providing the services specified.

    2. Community Fibre Data will only be stored in authorised systems, applications and databases and must not be downloaded or transferred from such systems, saved locally, or moved onto supplier systems without approval from Community Fibre.

    3. Community Fibre Data will not be written down, photographed, printed, or photocopied.

    4. Only Community Fibre approved note taking mechanisms such as the Knowledge notepad function will be employed within the Contact Centre Environment with such mechanisms being wiped after a period agreed by Community Fibre.

    5. Community Fibre Data will not be transferred onto removable media under any circumstances. Removable media drives within endpoints will be disabled or controlled to prevent such transfer.

    6. The use of any email service is prohibited unless this has been approved by Community Fibre. Where email services are approved, technical restrictions will prevent these email services being accessible outside of Community Fibre approved locations. The domains of incoming and outgoing emails will be restricted to only those approved by Community Fibre.

    7. Internet access will be restricted to only Community Fibre approved URLs and Domains.

    8. If two headsets or phones are being used (i.e., for training or monitoring purposes) both lines will be recorded in case the secondary staff member takes over the call.

    9. Calls to physical or softphones cannot be transferred or diverted to a mobile or external number.

docs.title: Physical Security
docs.text:
1. Appropriate physical security controls shall be in place to prevent unauthorised access to the Contact Centre and BPO Environment and Community Fibre data held within it. This will include but is not limited to:

a) Physical perimeter security controls such as gates, fences, and manned entry points;

b) A documented and enforced clear desk policy;

c) A requirement for all staff to visibly wear ID badges at all times within the Contact Centre

d) Control of entry points by access control mechanisms such as turnstiles to prevent tailgating;

e) physical security zoning with appropriate access control between sensitive areas such as the contact centre floor, data centres, comms rooms and back-office areas to ensure that there is no inappropriate access to areas where customer data is processed;

f) Locking screens when away from desk or automatically when there is a period of inactivity e.g., 10 minutes;

g) Computer screens which will be used to access customer data must not be visible from outside the building. Where this is not possible privacy screens will be used to restrict the view of such screens;

h) CCTV will be in operation and monitored within the Contact Centre. The footage must be stored for a minimum of 90-days or as per the legal jurisdiction requirements;

i) Printing will be disabled;

j) Any Laptops used will be secured to the desks at the working location; and

k) Laptops are prohibited to be taken off-site unless approved by Community Fibre in writing.

1.  A physical perimeter (outer) and security (inner) assessment
    shall be conducted on an annual basis as part of the risk
    assessment required at 3.1 of this appendix.

docs.title: Access Management
docs.text:
1. Staff with access to Community Fibre Data must undergo (and then repeat regularly) security awareness training along with all other necessary training to ensure that they can use systems storing Community Fibre Data competently prior to being given access to ensure the security and integrity of Community Fibre Data.

    2. Appropriate processes and technical controls shall be in place to ensure that physical and logical access to the contact centre environment and Community Fibre Data is restricted to authorised staff on the basis of the principles of "least privilege", appropriate segregation of duties and "need to know".

    3. Role based, and where possible workflow based, access will be implemented to limit access to excessive amounts of data.

    4. Multi-factor authentication will be implemented for access to systems and application which will allow access to Community Fibre Customer Personal Data.

    5. All contact centre and BPO staff accessing Community Fibre Data will do so using a unique account linked to their identity which has been verified through appropriate background checks.

    6. Contact centre and BPO staff will not access Community Fibre Data through generic or shared accounts and will not share unique accounts, passwords or other means of authentication which allow access with other staff members, contractors, contingent workers, or any other person.

    7. Where a member of staff leaves the organisation in an unplanned manner, for example due to gross misconduct, their access shall be disabled immediately. Any known passwords shall be reset.

    8. Where a member of staff is absent from work for 3 working days without explanation their access must be disabled.

    9. Where a member of staff is absent from work for longer than 30 days for any reason their access should be disabled.

    10. Reviews of access rights will be conducted at a minimum every 6 months to ensure that all staff access and permissions are appropriate to the role assigned to them. Where inappropriate access is identified this shall be removed in a timely fashion in line with 11.6.

docs.title: Monitoring and Compliance
docs.text:
1. Managers or a responsible person will perform and document a review of the call centre and BPO environment including physical, process based and technical security controls on quarterly basis to ensure that those controls are operating effectively. This should include but is not limited to those requirements set out within this schedule.

a) The results of such reviews shall be made available to Community Fibre representatives on request.

b) An action plan shall be developed to address any deficiencies identified and progress reported to Community Fibre representatives, along with levels of non-compliance identified because of the review.

1.  A set of customer information security metrics will be
    developed, implemented, and reported on to Community Fibre
    representatives as part of regular Monthly Business Reviews.

2.  System logging, monitoring, and alerting must be implemented to
    ensure that any fraudulent activity, unauthorised access, or
    potential exfiltration of data is identified and acted upon.

3.  Community Fibre reserves the right to monitor electronic records
    and logs pertaining to the activities undertaken in the Contact
    Centre and BPO to deliver the services to Community Fibre. This
    could include emails, internet browsing, application logs and
    any other log that is deemed appropriate to the service.

This standard will be reviewed on an annual basis to ensure it reflects current Community Fibre working practices, industry standards and legislative developments.

docs.text:
1. Where the service or services to be provided relate to the provision of a Cloud solution (including IaaS, PaaS, SaaS or FaaS) for use by:

a) Community Fibre Group employees; or

b) Third-party staff authorised to access Community Fibre data or IT systems (examples include contractors, consultants, outsourced provider personnel and vendor support personnel);

the Supplier is required, in accordance with the Center for Internet Security's recommendations, to agree to the responsibilities of a "Cloud Provider" as detailed in the table below.
