docs.title: Leadership and commitment
docs.text:
Community Fibre Limited's senior management team are committed to the development and implementation of an ISMS Policy and Information Security Management System which are both compatible with the strategic direction and the context of the organisation. In summary, the senior management team will ensure that:

  • The company has a designated senior management representative who is responsible for the maintenance and review of the Management System.

  • The ongoing activities of Community Fibre Limited are reviewed regularly and that any required corrective action is adequately implemented and reviewed to establish an effective preventative process.

  • Measurement of our performance against our declared Information Security Objectives is undertaken.

  • Resources needed for the system are available and employees have the necessary training, skills, and equipment to effectively carry out their work.

  • Internal audits are conducted regularly to review progress and assist in the improvement of processes and procedures.

  • Objectives are reviewed and, if necessary amended, at Management Review meetings and the performance communicated to all staff.

  • The information security policy and objectives are established in line with the strategic direction of the organisation and that intended outcome(s) are achieved.

  • The management system is integrated into the organisations business processes.

  • Communication covering the importance of the effective management system and conformance to the management system requirements is in place.

  • Continual improvement is promoted.

  • The contribution of persons involved in the effectiveness of the management system is achieved by engaging, directing, and supporting persons and other management roles within their area of responsibility.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text: The ISMS Policy of Community Fibre Limited is documented and accessible to all staff and contractors in the following location: Approved (ISP003-Information Security Policy)

docs.title: Organisational roles, responsibilities, and authorities
docs.text: Community Fibre Limited employee contracts together with job descriptions ensure that the appropriate personnel are in place to cover the whole context of the organisation and strategy of the business.

docs.title: Current Roles and Staffing
docs.text:
The following table lists the individuals currently performing the key roles within the ISMS. The Information Security Officer is responsible for ensuring that this table remains current.

Title Name Authority

5.3.1.1 Executive Various Senior organisational management

5.3.1.2 ISMS Board Various Ownership of the ISMS

5.3.1.3 Senior Chris Williams Technical and IT operational Management Security (CIO) leadership Representative

5.3.1.4 Information Chris Steytler Head of Security Security Officer

5.3.1.5 HR Director Aimee Haller People, competence, and legal leadership

5.3.1.6 Information Third-party Expert knowledge -- ISO27001 Security Internal Supplier -- Auditor Saepio

5.3.1.7 Managed Third-party Security monitoring and Detection and Response Supplier -- ANS response (MDR)

5.3.1.8 Senior Network Martin Low Network security leadership Security Engineer

docs.title: Executive
docs.text:
• Provide visible management support and commitment.

  • Approve and sign off on policies, e.g., Information Security Policy.

  • Ultimate ownership of Information Security risks, including the Community Fibre Limited risk management framework and associated corporate governance.

docs.title: ISMS Board
docs.text:
• Hold overall ownership of the ISMS.

  • Report to the Executive through the Senior Management Security Representative, with the Information Security Officer and Information Security Internal Auditor carrying out a more detailed review and monitoring function on behalf of the ISMS Board.

  • Establish and communicate Information Security and Risk Management roles and responsibilities across Community Fibre Limited, to ensure Information Security and Risk Management activities are incorporated into the decision-making processes by all staff.

  • Ensuring that the organisation pursues sound and proper policies in relation to Information Security & Risk Management and that these are clearly communicated to all staff.

  • Providing senior management support and leadership on Information Security & Risk Management.

  • Review, discuss and direct escalated risks, audit findings, Security Improvement Actions and other issues pertaining to Information Security that could affect corporate strategy.

  • Make formal decisions following reviews of progress made in addressing existing risks and Security Improvement Actions. As part of this, the ISMS Board is responsible for reviewing the Risk Assessment (including Risk Treatment Plans and the Risk Acceptance Register) at each convened meeting, and recording continuing acceptance of risks, with day-to-day responsibilities being delegated to the Information Security Officer.

  • Periodically review the ISMS audit reports to ensure the continuing effectiveness of the Internal Audit Compliance Framework.

  • Address any trends in non-conformities that can be identified.

  • Review and analyse incident information provided by Information Security Officer, Information Security Internal Auditor and Heads of Department.

docs.title: Senior Management Security Representative
docs.text:
• ISMS sponsor and chair of ISMS Board.

  • Report any issues and risks as well as other notable results of the meetings to the Executive to secure on-going senior management buy-in and commitment throughout the lifetime of the ISMS.

  • Responsible for ensuring that the annual ISO 27001 ISMS Management Review is carried out appropriately and in a timely fashion.

  • Responsible for ensuring that the required participants attend the annual Management Review.

docs.title: General Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Operational Chair for ISMS Board meetings.

  • To act as representative of the ISMS Board.

  • Hold operational responsibility for the ISMS -- carry out detailed review and monitoring function on behalf of the ISMS Board (together with Information Security Internal Auditor).

  • Notify the appropriate ISMS Board attendees with at least 10 working days' notice.

  • Publish minutes of ISMS Board meeting and distribute to all attendees.

  • Responsibility for updating the ISMS and monitoring compliance.

  • Provide expert advice to support Heads of Department and their teams to help them make informed decisions regarding Information Security related matters, including risk and appropriate Security Improvement Actions.

docs.title: Risk Management Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Hold operational day to day responsibility for reviewing and maintaining the Risk Assessment, Risk Treatment Plan and Risk Acceptance Register.

  • Ensure that the Information Security risk process is continually assessed for appropriateness and to ensure that it is being adhered to.

  • Ensuring the implementation, co-ordination, and monitoring of the Risk Management process and for reporting to the ISMS Board.

  • Maintain a watching brief over the ISMS and produce an Annual Information Security Risk Management report for the Information Security Internal Auditor and ISMS Board.

docs.title: Security Improvement Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Coordinates and maintains organisational Security Improvement Program and Plan.

  • Identifies organisational Security Improvement Actions and coordinates resolution through liaison with relevant Business Units, Heads of Department, and 3rd party supplier(s).

  • Monitors and report progress of organisational Security Improvement Actions and overall Security Improvement Program at ISMS Board meetings.

  • Work with Business Units, Heads of Department, and 3rd party supplier(s) in resolving and monitoring progress of SIP actions.

docs.title: Audit Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Owner of the ISMS Audit Framework.

  • Collate audit information in line with audit requirements and report findings to the ISMS Board. This responsibility may be delegated to the Information Security Internal Auditor.

docs.title: Incident Management Responsibilities
docs.text: • Analyse available incident information to identify trends and notable lessons from both successes and failures and report findings to the ISMS Board.

docs.title: HR Director
docs.text:
• Responsible for establishing, maintaining, and enforcing starter / leaver / job role change process, such as vetting and retrieval of assets as well as process supporting the review and revocation of access rights.

  • Responsible for overseeing that job role descriptions appropriately state all relevant Information Security responsibilities.

  • Create competency levels based on job role descriptions and identify and address training needs.

  • Support the inclusion of Information Security training at induction of all employees.

  • Support the Information Security Officer with disciplinary matters.

  • Ensure security responsibilities are a formal part of the contract of employment for all employees.

  • Report relevant issues to the Information Security Officer.

docs.title: Information Security Internal Auditor
docs.text:
• Carry out a more detailed review and monitoring function on behalf of the ISMS Board and Information Security Officer.

  • Carry out regular compliance audits in line with the Audit Framework and report results to the Information Security Officer and the ISMS Board.

  • Review the Information Security Risk Management process and the nature and extent of risks within the ISO 27001 scope.

  • Set and agree appropriate policies for internal control with the Information Security Officer to ensure that Information Security risk is effectively managed.

  • Annually review the Information Security Risk Management process and strategy and report to the Information Security Officer and the ISMS Board on its efficacy.

  • Seek evidence on an on-going basis of process being in place and followed, which ensures that trends and notable lessons are being learned from incidents (both successes and failures), including revisiting the risk assessment and treatment plan.

docs.title: Managed Detection and Response (MDR)
docs.text:
• Provide 24/7 managed security operations function.

  • Provide Threat Intelligence (TI) information about current cyber threats to the CFL networks, services, and IT estate.

  • Perform proactive, iterative, and human-centric identification of cyber threats that have evaded existing security controls.

  • Turn threat intelligence into programmatic detection rules within the SOC tools which in turn are used to identify suspicious behaviour from within CFL systems and services.

  • Responding to security events by investigating the root cause of an event. The main objective is to determine whether an event should be escalated into a security incident.

  • Security incident management.

  • Identify vulnerabilities within the estate.

  • Detecting and responding to Insider Threat.

docs.title: Senior Network Security Engineer
docs.text:
• Design, implement, and maintain network security architectures, including firewalls, intrusion detection/prevention systems (IDS/IPS), VPNs, and secure access controls, in alignment with ISO 27001 Annex A.8.20 (Network Security).

  • Conduct regular vulnerability assessments, penetration testing, and security audits on network infrastructure to identify and mitigate risks.

  • Monitor network traffic for anomalies, potential breaches, and emerging threats, collaborating with the Managed Detection and Response (MDR) team for real-time response.

  • Develop and update network security policies, procedures, and standards to ensure compliance with ISMS requirements and relevant regulations (e.g., UK NIS Regulations for critical infrastructure).

  • Support incident response activities for network-related security events, including root cause analysis and post-incident reviews to inform Security Improvement Actions.

  • Ensure secure configuration and hardening of network devices (e.g., routers, switches, load balancers) and integration with overall ISMS controls.

  • Contribute to risk assessments and treatment plans, particularly for network-specific risks such as DDoS attacks, unauthorised access, or climate-induced disruptions to physical network infrastructure (e.g., flooding impacting fiber optic cables).

  • Provide technical expertise and training to IT and security teams on network security best practices and emerging technologies.

  • Liaise with third-party suppliers and partners to ensure secure network interconnections and supply chain security.

  • Report network security metrics, findings, and recommendations to the Information Security Officer and ISMS Board for ongoing monitoring and improvement.

docs.title: Planning
docs.text: 1. []{#_6.1_Actions_to .anchor}

docs.title: Actions to address risks and opportunities.
General
docs.text:
We have identified the risks and opportunities that are relevant to our business management system considering the issues covered in sections 4.1 (context) and 4.2 (needs and expectations of interested parties) of this document. Identified risks and opportunities are documented and tracked in the "ISMS Risks & Treatments" section of the ISMS management system (ISMS.online). Risks are identified together with a rating as to the importance (Impact X Likelihood) of the risk. The associated potential consequence & mitigation of the risk is also noted together with any new opportunities that we have identified.

The controls identified in this document feed into our risk treatment plan (Statement of Applicability), which has been designed and implemented using the main headings within the standard (Annex A, Table A.1 -- Control objectives and controls) as a guide to establish that all controls required have been considered and that there are no omissions. The document identifies controls to mitigate risks following the process of identification, analysis, and evaluation.

docs.title: Information security risk assessment
docs.text:
A recognised process of likelihood and impact analysis is considered for risk assessment, considering the potential loss of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information for the impact scoring.

A detailed risk management policy is available here: Approved (ISP033-Risk Management Policy)

docs.title: Information security risk treatment
docs.text: Treatments are documented as required in terms of free text notes, tasks, discussions, or documents, including where appropriate, links to relevant policies and controls as part of the wider system.

docs.title: Changes to the ISMS
docs.text: Change to the ISMS including scope and controls will be planned, reviewed and approved by the ISMS Board.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
Community Fibre Limited determines and provides the resources needed for the establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of the management system. This is evidenced by:

  • Leadership resource commitment expressed in (5.1) and (9.3)

  • Providing the resources for the ISMS per (A.5.3 - Information security roles and responsibilities)

  • Activity owners and supporting team members for each one of the requirements, policies, and controls for the standards we have chosen to apply.

  • Procurement and creation of the ISMS.online environment for overall policy control and the enabling infrastructure to deliver work such as ISMS Board reviews per (9.3), Internal Audits per 9.2, Nonconformities and Corrective Actions per (10.2) and Risk Assessment & Treatment per (6.1).

  • Specific resources allocated for risk management (6.1), internal audits (9.2), nonconformities, corrective actions, performance evaluation and ongoing improvement and specialist areas of work such as managing information security incidents.

  • Mechanisms for efficiently communicating and engaging all staff and supply chain resources in the scope of the management system such as staff induction sessions, security awareness training and communications via channels such as BambooHR and email.

  • Resource investment in the ISMS.online management system platform for the professional implementation and ongoing delivery of the management system to ensure that our limited physical resources are optimised and focused.

Our resources involved in the establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement in the management system are senior experienced staff, experts in their fields. They have all read around the subject matter for each standard, hold certifications where appropriate and recognise the importance of staying up to date with developments in their respective fields. This includes training and development as required, both informally e.g., online personal development, and formal training programs with certification at the end.

Harnessing best practice tools such as ISMS.online with built-in competence for related areas e.g., risk assessment and supplier management are also evidenced throughout the management system.

The organisation's culture and values push us towards continual improvement. Information security is a thread like commercial development or organisation change that we constantly work on in our day jobs. This is also evidenced where we take the opportunity to further improve practices by following up research from staff, staying abreast of what works in the firm and elsewhere.

docs.title: Competence
docs.text:
All employees have the training and skills needed to meet their job requirements. All employees are monitored on an ongoing basis to identify any training and development needs. Competences and training needs are identified / satisfied by using:

  • Formal job descriptions which set out the competences required.

  • Contracts of employment which set out contractual and legal requirements.

  • Induction checklists to ensure / check understanding.

  • Development plans to set objectives.

  • Performance reviews to ensure / check levels of competence.

  • A training / competency matrix.

docs.title: Awareness
docs.text:
We ensure that all employees are aware of all policies and their contribution to the effectiveness of the Management System through:

  • Companywide communications (i.e., email) campaigns

  • BambooHR

  • Employee Intranet

  • Awareness training at induction and then at set intervals

  • Linking associated information security policies to security notifications (pop-ups) via business systems (i.e., M365)

docs.title: Communication
docs.text: This section describes formal communications regarding information security that relates to elements within scope of the ISMS. We need to ensure that relevant issues (i.e., new policies or significant changes) are communicated to stakeholders clearly and consistently so that people have the necessary information and guidance to carry out their responsibilities for information security.

docs.title: Recipients and triggers
docs.text: Information security management communications are sent to all stakeholders who are directly affected by the matter being communicated or with responsibilities for any affected procedures.

docs.title: Communication Scope
docs.text:
Information security management communications of new and updated policies should be communicated in a manner that is clear and comprehensive and may include some of the following:

  1. The purpose or objective of the policy.

  2. Description of the policy as it relates to the recipient.

  3. Responsibilities for implementing and managing the policy.

  4. Feasible timeframe for implementation.

  5. Review plan for the policy.

  6. Opportunity for queries and comments.

However, information must not be distributed where doing so may cause a compromise to information security.

docs.title: Communication Responsibilities
docs.text: Effective communications about information security are assigned to the following roles:

docs.title: Senior Management Security Representative (CIO)
docs.text:
1. To communicate the importance of effective information security management and of conforming to ISMS requirements, and the consequences of not doing so.

  2. To review communication policies for making information available to relevant people in a timely manner and via appropriate channels.

  3. To ensure the ISMS Board has the relevant information.

  4. To maintain open communication channels and to listen to feedback and comments from the business.

docs.title: Information Security Officer (Head of Security)
docs.text:
1. To maintain the ISMS.

  2. To carry out internal audits of policies processes and systems relating to the ISMS.

  3. To ensure policies, procedures are updated and communicated to those who need to know.

  4. To maintain risk, non-conformity, incident, and vulnerability registers.

  5. To communicate risks and issues to the ISMS Board that could undermine information security.

  6. To communicate good security practices.

  7. To monitor and record progress against outstanding incidents and actions, vulnerabilities, risk treatments or security improvements.

docs.title: Executive
docs.text:
1. To communicate regularly with their team, preferably face to face, to ensure information relating to the ISMS is available, understood and up to date.

  2. To ensure they and their team are maintaining ISMS records.

  3. To listen to feedback from their team and users and to keep the ISMS Board informed.

  4. To communicate the outcomes of any ISMS Risk Assessment or Risk Treatment Plan.

docs.title: Community Fibre IT and Security Operations staff
docs.text:
1. To ensure they are informed and have access to information to be as effective as possible in their role.

  2. To ensure they are maintaining good communication practice as set out in this document.

  3. To maintain user, project, information and physical and/or virtual assets inventories.

  4. To keep line managers, colleagues, and users aware of up-to-date information

docs.title: Community Fibre staff
docs.text:
1. To keep the Information Security Officer informed about their needs for data handling.

  2. To address any information security requirements raised with them (by i.e., Line manager, Information Security Officer, or the Executive team) and to communicate the outcome (for example, by completing any Cyber Awareness or GDPR training).

docs.title: Community Fibre suppliers and contractors
docs.text:
1. To ensure they are maintaining good communication practice as set out in this document.

  2. To address any information security requirements raised with them and to communicate the outcome.

  3. To keep line managers and Community Fibre internal contacts aware of up-to-date information.

docs.title: Communication Channels
docs.text:
1. The intended audience and their location will determine the most suitable channel, and the following factors need to be considered:

  2. Location -- a shared office may restrict what can be communicated. A remote user may limit the channels available for use.

  3. Role -- a person's role and relevant expertise may influence whether a more suited to interaction and feedback is appropriate.

  4. Impact -- a direct conversation, training sessions or detailed documentation may be more suitable than email communication or notification for people whose daily work is affected by the issue being communicated.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Community Fibre Limited demonstrates documented compliance to ISO 27001 (or any other standard in line with Annex SL Structure) through this ISMS (which includes processes & procedures) on an electronic system which is available on the company intranet to all employees. All information is read only and only accessible via the document owner for amendment.

The ISMS refers to Community Fibre Limited's ISO9001 IMS document - IMS04 Documents & Communication for document control. (IMS04 Documents & Communication)

docs.title: Creating and updating
docs.text:
The ISMS is identified as follows:

  • ISP -- Information Security Management System Policy

  • ISPR - Information Security Management System Procedure

  • ISD - Information Security Management System Document

The numbering process will contain the above identifier and a number which identifies the respective procedure:

ISMS policies will be identified as ISP001; ISP002; etc.

To maintain the ongoing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of documented information, including all ISMS policies, procedures, and supporting documents:

  • Policy review: Policy document owners will conduct reviews to evaluate content against current risks, organisational context, regulatory requirements, and performance metrics. Reviews involve assessing for updates needed due to changes in internal or external issues, risk assessments, incidents, audit findings, or management review outcomes. Proposed changes must be documented (e.g., via change logs including author, date, and description of modifications), reviewed by relevant stakeholders, and approved by top management or authorised personnel before implementation.

  • Policy review frequency: All documented information will be reviewed at planned intervals, at least annually, or upon significant changes (e.g., organisational restructuring, new threats, or legal updates).

docs.title: Control of documented information
docs.text:
All procedures, documents and forms that are part of the ISMS are identified in ISMS.online.

Automatic backup copies are taken by SharePoint Online where the Approved Document Register resides. These backups avoid the loss of confidentiality, improper use, or loss of integrity.

All approved policy documents are uploaded to and available to all staff in BambooHR. Contract and agency staff must be provided with relevant copies of policies.

docs.title: Classification of documented information
docs.text: The ISMS refers to Community Fibre Limited's ISO9001 IMS document - IMS04 Documents & Communication for document control and classification. (IMS04 Documents & Communication)

docs.title: 8.1 Operational planning and control
docs.text:
Community Fibre Limited has determined the requirements and controls implemented for all processes needed to meet Information Security requirements and has implemented the actions described in section 6.1 (Actions to address risks and opportunities) of this ISMS. We will also implement plans to achieve ISMS objectives, as highlighted in sections 3 (Objectives) and 6.2 (Information security objectives and planning to achieve them) of this ISMS. We retain documented information to the extent necessary to have confidence that the processes have been carried out as planned. We shall control any planned changes and will review the consequences of unintended changes, taking action to mitigate any adverse effects.

Actions (i.e., incident response), activities (logging and monitoring) and projects undertaken by the Security Operations function are defined and documented in the Security Operations Framework (ISD001- Operational Security Framework). These tasks and their associated high-level specifications are generated to enforce information security, detect, and act on violations, and make security intrinsic to the company's future in both enhancing its reputation and avoiding criminal and civil actions, and supports the operation of the ISMS.

docs.title: 8.2 Information Security risk assessment
docs.text: In line with the criteria established in section 6.1.2 of this ISMS, we perform ISMS risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur. Documented information of the results of risk assessments is retained.

docs.title: 8.3 Information Security risk treatment
docs.text: The risk treatment is incorporated within Risks & Opportunities -- See Clause 6.1.

docs.title: 9.1 Monitoring, measurement, analysis, and evaluation
docs.text: Monitoring (see 6.2) is based on risk and is linked to the risk & opportunities register together with the risk assessments which are carried out. This is also monitored through internal audits (section 9.2) and management review (section 9.3) to ensure the effectiveness of the management system.

docs.title: 9.2 Internal Audit
docs.text:
An internal audit schedule is prepared on an annual basis year and covers the requirements of the ISO27001 standard. Internal audits are carried out through "risk or clause based" auditing. Appropriate personnel are allocated to complete the internal audits and must record appropriate evidence for completeness. All audits completed must be authorised by Senior Management as complete once any non-conforming areas have been dealt with (without any undue delay). Internal audit documentation must be kept and filed appropriately.

The ISMS management platform (ISMS.online) contains the ISO 27001 Audit Program (three years including GDPR) including ISMS internal audits 3-year plan.

docs.title: 9.3 Management review
docs.text:
Management reviews take place as a minimum on an annual basis. The attendees present are "Senior Management" and any other appropriate persons of the business.

All inputs / outputs are fully documented, and minutes captured in line with the requirements of the specific ISO standard in which Community Fibre Limited wish to be certified. Any actions arising from the meeting must be completed without any undue delay and appropriate evidence filed with the Management review documentation.

docs.title: 10.1 Continual Improvement
docs.text:
Continual Improvement will be ongoing through various elements of the Business Management System which is encompassed within this document. The list below is not exhaustive:

  • "ISMS Risks & Treatments" - ISMS management system (ISMS.online) (See Clause 5.1, 6.1)

  • ISMS Policy and objectives

  • Customer satisfaction

  • Internal audits

  • Third-party external audits

  • Management reviews

docs.title: 10.2 Nonconformity and corrective action
docs.text:
Should any non-conformances occur or be identified then an internal audit report / non-conformance report must be completed to ensure that a full analysis of the problem is resolved. A summary of all actions will be maintained within the "ISMS Corrective Actions & Improvements" queue in Jira. The corrective action plan summary must be completed, as this then forms part of the Management Review meeting.

Should a nonconformity occur, including those arising from complaints, internal audits & external third-party assessment Community Fibre Limited designate the appropriate "Senior Management" representative to ensure that corrective action including root cause analysis is completed and implemented to avoid any further occurrences. This is then analysed and should the risk to the business pose to be "high" then this is then entered onto the "ISMS Risks & Treatments" section of the ISMS management system (ISMS.online) (See Clause 6.1) to assist in mitigating the risk to the business.

docs.title: The purpose of this document is to demonstrate the management board's commitment to information security and to provide the over-arching policy statements to which all subordinate policies and controls must adhere.
This document meets the following clauses:
Information Security Management System BS EN ISO/IEC 27001:2022 -- 5.2 Information security policy
Policy
docs.text:
The Board of Directors and management of Community Fibre Limited located at 77 Hatton Garden, London, EC1N 8JS operates primarily in the business of the provisioning of broadband internet services.

We are committed to preserving the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all the physical and electronic information and information-related assets to meet the purpose and goals of the organisation.

Information and information security requirements will be aligned with the organisation's business goals and will consider the internal and external issues affecting the organisation and the requirements of interested parties. Information security objectives for the ISMS are set in line with business strategy and outlined in ISMS manual. (ISP001-ISMS Mandatory Clauses)

The ISMS is intended as a mechanism for managing information security related risks and improving the organisation to help deliver its overall purpose and goals.

The ISMS management platform (ISMS.online), and our approach to risk management, provides the context for identifying, assessing, evaluating, and controlling information-related risks through the establishment and maintenance of an ISMS.

The approach taken towards Risk Assessment and Management, the Statement of Applicability and the wider requirements set out for meeting ISO 27001:2022 identify how information security and related risks are addressed.

The ISMS Board is chaired by the Head of Security and has ongoing senior representation from appropriate parts of the organisation. Other executives/specialists needed to support the ISMS framework and to periodically review the security policy and broader ISMS are invited in the ISMS Board meetings and complete relevant work as required, all of which is documented in accordance with the standard.

The ISMS Board is responsible for the overall management and maintenance of the risk treatment plan with specific risk management activity tasked to the appropriate owner within the organisation. Additional risk assessments may, where necessary, be carried out to determine appropriate controls for specific risks, for example during special projects that are completed within the context.

The ISMS Board review the effectiveness of the ISMS and, in line with the policy and procedures identified, seek to continuously improve the effectiveness of the ISMS through analysing audit results, and monitoring events and activity, all in the context of the business goals and risk treatment plan, and at least once a year. Controls are measured to ensure they are effective and achieve continual improvement.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
In this policy and the related set of policies contained within the management platform that incorporate our ISMS, 'information security' is defined as:

"Preserving

This means that all relevant Interested Parties have, and will be made aware of, their responsibilities that are defined in their job descriptions or contracts to act in accordance with the requirements of the ISMS. The consequences of not doing so are described in the Code of Conduct. All relevant Interested Parties will receive information security awareness training and more specialised resources will receive appropriately specialised information security training.

the availability,

This means that information and associated assets should be accessible to authorised users when required and therefore physically secure. The environment must be resilient, and the organisation must be able to detect and respond rapidly to incidents or events that threaten the continued availability of assets, systems, and information.

confidentiality,

This involves ensuring that information is only accessible to those authorised to access it and preventing both deliberate and accidental unauthorised access to the organisation and relevant Interested Parties information, proprietary knowledge, assets, and other systems in scope.

and integrity

This involves safeguarding the accuracy and completeness of information and processing methods, and therefore requires preventing deliberate or accidental, partial, or complete, destruction or unauthorised modification, of either physical assets or electronic data.

of information and other relevant assets

The information can include digital information, printed or written on paper, transmitted by any means, or spoken in conversation, as well as information stored electronically. Assets include all information-based processing devices owned by the organisation or those of relevant Interested Parties and BYOD in scope that are processing organisation related information.

of our organisation."

The organisation and relevant Interested Parties that are within the scope of the ISMS have signed up to our security policy and accepted our ISMS.

This information security policy was approved by the CEO and is issued on a version-controlled basis under the approval of the ISMS Board.

docs.title: Document Objective
docs.text:
This Access Control Policy provides the overarching framework for managing access to Community Fibre's information assets, networks, systems, and facilities. It ensures access is appropriate, proportionate to risks, and aligned with business and compliance requirements.

This policy serves as the primary reference for access controls within the ISMS, supported by more detailed policy documents.

This document meets the following clauses:

  • ISO/IEC 27001:2022 -- A.5.15: Access control

  • NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF) v3.1 - B2 Identity and Access Control

  • The Electronic Communications(Security Measures) Regulations 2022 -- Access controls for security-critical functions, including least privilege, unique credentials, and monitoring

docs.title: Supporting policies and documents
docs.text:
• Information Classification and Handling Policy (ISP037)

  • Information Access Rights Policy (ISP011)

  • Password Management Policy (ISP040)

  • Identity Management Policy (ISP012)

  • Privileged Access Rights Policy (ISP013)

  • User Registration Policy (ISP014)

  • Physical Security Standard (ISD006)

  • Statement of Applicability (current version)

  • Employee Handbook (Community Fibre - Employee Handbook 2023 - v3.pdf)

docs.title: Scope and principles
docs.text: This policy applies to all access, physical and logical, to Community Fibre\'s information assets, networks, systems, services, and facilities, including those managed by employees, contractors, third parties, and automated processes. It covers the full lifecycle of access rights, ensuring alignment with business needs, information security risks, and regulatory requirements, including the Telecommunications (Security) Act 2021 and its accompanying Code of Practice.

docs.title: Topic-specific approach
docs.text: Access controls are implemented based on the sensitivity of assets (per ISP037 -- Information Classification and Handling Policy) and risk assessments. This includes physical controls for facilities and logical controls for systems, with a focus on security-critical functions in telecom infrastructure.

docs.title: Supporting policies
docs.text:
Detailed procedures are outlined in supporting documents:

  1. Information Access Rights Policy (ISP011): Outlines the requirements for granting access rights to various information assets based on employees\' roles and responsibilities. It aims to establish consistency between the data and systems to which access is given and the type of access rights assigned.

  2. Password Management Policy (ISP040): Mandates the use of strong, unique passwords for each user, based on up-to-date recognised best practice, including the use of Multi-Factor Authentication, guidance for the creation of secure passwords and secure handling guidelines.

  3. Identity Management Policy (ISP012): Governs the creation, maintenance, and revocation of user identities within our systems. It also includes provisions for role-based access control (RBAC) to ensure authorised access privileges are granted based on predefined job functions and responsibilities.

  4. Privileged Access Rights Policy (ISP042): Defines the process for granting, monitoring, and auditing access privileges and Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) for users with privileged access rights. We closely monitor users with privileged access to prevent any compromise of our Access Control function.

  5. User Registration Policy (ISP043): Sets guidelines for onboarding and offboarding employees and other entities. When granting access, we follow a structured, formal access request and authorisation process, ensuring documented approval from the appropriate personnel.

  6. Physical Security Standard (ISD006): Set guidelines for physical entry and perimeter controls to prevent unauthorised access, damage, or interference with information assets and infrastructure.

docs.title: Logging & Monitoring
docs.text:
There is a duty to implement measures to monitor security-critical functions in public electronic communications networks or services, to detect any security breaches. (The Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022 Reg 6(2)(a)).

All access activities are logged and monitored:

  • Logical access logs include authentication attempts, changes, and anomalies.

  • Physical access logs track entry/exit.

  • Account and assigned role or permissions reviews occur every 6 months.

  • Incidents are investigated by Security Operations.

docs.title: Training & Awareness
docs.text:
All users receive training on access controls upon onboarding and annually:

  • There is a duty to ensure competence of responsible persons (The Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022 Reg 13(2)(a)).

  • Specialised training for privileged users.

docs.title: Consequences of non-compliance with this policy
docs.text: Any non-compliance with or breach of policy may lead to investigation and action in line with the organisational Disciplinary Policy (CFL Employee Handbook 2023 v.3).

docs.title: Document Objective
docs.text:
This Information Access Rights Policy outlines the requirements for managing access rights to Community Fibre Limited\'s information assets, ensuring they are granted, reviewed, and revoked in a controlled manner. It supports the overarching Access Control Policy (ISP010-Access Control Policy) by focusing specifically on information access rights, while complementing other supporting policies:

  • ISP012-Identity Management Policy

  • ISP040-Password Management Policy

  • ISP014-User Registration Policy

  • ISP013-Privileged Access Rights Policy

This document meets the following clauses:

  • ISO/IEC 27001:2022 -- A.5.15: Access control

  • ISO/IEC 27002:2022 -- A.5.18: Access rights

  • The Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022 -- Regulation 8 (Access controls for security-critical functions) and Code of Practice (3.1--3.7)

Access rights to information assets are managed to protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability, based on the principles of \"need-to-know,\" \"least privilege,\" and role-based access control (RBAC). This policy applies to all employees, contractors, third parties, and systems handling Community Fibre information assets throughout their lifecycle.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text: The purpose of this policy is to ensure appropriate access to information networks and systems are provided in line with identified requirements and are adequate and proportionate for assessed information security risks.

docs.title: Scope and principles
docs.text:
This policy applies to all access rights related to information assets, including electronic and physical forms, across Community Fibre\'s networks, systems, and services. It encompasses user access, privileged access, and third-party access, with references to supporting policies for detailed procedures.

Key principles:

  • Need-to-Know

  • Least Privilege

  • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

  • Segregation of Duties

  • Information Classification Alignment

All access rights must consider the value, sensitivity, and risks associated with information assets, as identified through risk assessments.

docs.title: Access rights based on information classification
docs.text:
Access to information assets is governed by their classification (ISP037 -- Information Classification and Handling Policy). The following guidelines apply:

  • Public: Access is unrestricted but must be approved for release. No specific controls beyond standard authentication are required, but usage must comply with business policies.

  • Confidential: Access is limited to authorised personnel on a need-to-know basis. Default for most business-sensitive data (e.g., draft work, customer communications).

  • Requires RBAC with multi-factor authentication for remote access.

  • Storage and transfer must use approved systems (e.g., SharePoint, Teams), with encryption for removable media if approved.

  • Third-party sharing requires NDAs, DPAs (for PII), and owner approval.

  • Strictly Confidential: Access is restricted due to potential severe impact (e.g., PII, PCI data, intellectual property, critical infrastructure details).

  • Limited to essential personnel; requires explicit approval from the asset owner.

  • MFA mandatory; privileged access must use privileged access workstations (PAWs) for security-critical functions.

  • Storage on personal devices restricted; hard copies must be secured (e.g., locked cabinets) and not removed off site without permission.

  • PCI data handling follows PCI DSS guidelines in ISP037-Information Classification and Handling Policy, with no storage of sensitive elements (e.g., CVV) and encryption for transmission.

  • Passwords must be stored in an approved password manager.

  • Third-party access requires NDAs, DPAs, risk assessments, and logged approvals.

Information owners (ISP037 -- Information Classification and Handling Policy) are responsible for classifying assets and approving access rights.

docs.title: Access right process
docs.text:
1. Granting Access

  2. Access requests must be submitted via the IT Service Desk (itsupport@communityfibre.co.uk) or the Network Technology team with approval from the information asset/system owner or line manager.

  3. Access is provisioned using RBAC and automated tools where possible, aligned with user roles (ISP014-User Registration Policy for onboarding).

  4. For privileged access, follow the ISP013-Privileged Access Rights Policy, including segregation of duties and PAW usage.

  5. Third-party access requires signed NDA, contract and risk assessment.

  6. Reviewing Access:

  7. Access rights are reviewed at least every 6 months by IT Service Desk, Security Operations and Network Technology team, or upon role changes, or incidents.

  8. Reviews include validation against business needs, classification levels, and compliance with Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations requirements (e.g., logging of privileged access per Regulation 8(5)).

  9. Exceptions (e.g., shared IDs) must be documented, justified, and re-approved.

  10. Revoking Access:

  • Access is revoked immediately upon termination, role change, or security incident notification (e.g., from HR or Security Operations).

  • Automated de-provisioning is used where integrated; manual revocation is logged.

  • Unused accounts are disabled after 90 days of inactivity.

All actions are logged, auditable, and aligned with the ISP012-Identity Management Policy for user identities.

docs.title: User Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Users must only access information required for their roles and report any unauthorised access or anomalies immediately to Security Operations.

  • Authentication information (e.g., passwords) must be kept confidential (reference ISP040-Password Management Policy).

  • Users are accountable for actions under their assigned IDs and must comply with training on access controls.

docs.title: Regulatory requirements
docs.text:
Access requirements under the Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations and its Code of Practice include:

  • Security-critical functions: Access is restricted using least privilege, phishing resistant MFA, and privileged access workstations for high-risk activities (Reg 8(2)(b), 8(4), Reg 4(4)(a) [2]; CoP para 3.4--3.13, M11.08 [3])

  • Remote administrative access: Limited to UK-based or managed devices; third-party remote administration via jump boxes only (Reg 3(3)(f), 4(4)(a) [2], 5(2); CoP M2.01, M10.30 [3])

  • Logging and Monitoring: All access to security-critical information is logged, with unique credentials and regular reviews (Reg 6(3)(a-d), 8(2)(b),(d), 8(4), 8(5)(b),(c)) [2].

  • Risk-Based Controls: Access rights are proportionate to risks, including from third parties (Reg 8(2) (d-e), Reg 11(b)) [2].

Non-compliance with these requirements will result in regulatory reporting obligations.

docs.title: Document Objective
docs.text:
This Identity Management Policy outlines the requirements for managing user and system identities at Community Fibre Limited, ensuring secure provisioning, maintenance, and deprovisioning of identities. It supports the overarching ISP034-Access Control Policy by focusing on identity lifecycle management, while complementing other supporting policies such as the Information Access Rights Policy (ISP011), Password Management Policy (ISP040), User Registration Policy (ISP014-User Registration Policy), and Privileged Access Rights Policy (ISP013-Privileged Access Rights Policy).

This document meets the following clauses:

  • ISO/IEC 27001:2022 -- A.5.16: Identity management

  • The Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022 -- Regulation 8 (Access controls for security-critical functions) and Code of Practice (3.1--3.7)

docs.title: Scope and principles
docs.text:
This policy applies to all identities (user, system, and service accounts) used to access Community Fibre\'s information assets, networks, systems, and services, including those managed for employees, contractors, third parties, and automated processes. It covers the full identity lifecycle and applies throughout the asset lifecycle.

Key principles, informed by NCSC guidance:

  • All users and systems must have unique, traceable identities to ensure accountability.

  • Identity controls are proportionate to the sensitivity of assets (per ISP037 -- Information Classification and Handling Policy) and assessed risks.

  • Identities are bound to roles with minimal access required.

  • Automation should be used for provisioning and deprovisioning to reduce errors and delays.

  • Prevent conflicts by separating identity management functions.

  • Regularly review, auditing of identities and threat hunting to detect anomalies.

Identity management is handled by IT Service Desk, Security Operations, Network Technology and HR, with oversight from the ISMS Board.

docs.title: Identity Lifecycle Management
docs.text:
The identity lifecycle includes provisioning, management, and deprovisioning, aligned with joiners, movers, and leavers processes.

  1. Provisioning

  2. New identities are created upon formal request (e.g., from HR for employees or contracts for third parties), with verification of the individual\'s or system\'s legitimacy.

  3. Background checks are completed by HR.

  4. Identities are bound to roles via Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), integrated with an Identity Provider (e.g., Microsoft Entra ID) for automated provisioning.

  5. Third-party identities require contracts and/or NDAs before provisioning.

  6. All new identities must use unique credentials, avoid default password, and enable MFA where applicable (reference ISP040-Password Management Policy).

  7. Management and Maintenance

  8. Identities are maintained through regular reviews (at least every 6 months) to ensure alignment with current roles and business needs.

  9. Changes (e.g., role movers) trigger immediate updates via formal requests, adjusting access rights accordingly (reference - ISD006-Joiner Mover Leaver Process).

  10. Authentication methods must match risk levels: Passwords for low-risk; MFA, certificates, or biometrics for higher-risk (e.g., remote access, privileged functions).

  11. Privileged identities require separate accounts from standard ones, with additional controls like privileged access workstations (PAWs) for security critical functions (reference Privileged Access Rights Policy).

  12. System and service identities (e.g., for APIs, operational technology systems) must be restricted, logged, and reviewed periodically.

  13. Deprovisioning

  14. Identities are revoked immediately upon termination, role change, or contract end, triggered by HR notifications or security incidents.

  15. Automated deprovisioning is used where possible; manual processes must be logged and confirmed.

  16. Dormant identities (inactive for 90 days) are disabled and reviewed for deletion.

  17. Ensure all associated access rights, credentials, and data are removed or transferred securely.

docs.title: Authentication, authorisation and audit
docs.text:
• Authentication or verification of an identity claim shall use factors including passwords, MFA, certificates, or biometrics. Strength must align with asset classification (e.g., MFA mandatory for Confidential and Strictly Confidential access).

  • Authorisation or determination of what the authenticated identity can do, shall be based on RBAC, least privilege, and need-to-know. Independent confirmation required for critical actions (e.g., code reviews, support tickets).

  • Operational technology in network infrastructure must be isolated from IT systems; avoid \"browse up\" (accessing higher-trust from lower) and monitor cross-boundary communications.

  • Remote authentication must consider device and location trust, with restrictions for non-UK or unmanaged devices.

  • All identity-related activities (e.g., logins, changes) must be logged, linked to unique users, and monitored for anomalies by the SOC and Security Operations.

  • Conduct periodic audits (every 6 months) and continuous vulnerability assessments on IAM systems.

  • Suspicious activity (e.g., unusual access times) must trigger alerts and investigations.

docs.title: Technologies and systems
docs.text:
• Business systems shall use centralised identity systems (e.g., Entra ID), following best practise secure administration recommendations and Privileged Identity Management to manage access to privileged roles.

  • Operational systems utilising LDAP and RADIUS for authentication and authorisation, ensuring secure configurations such as encryption (e.g., LDAPS, protected RADIUS communications) to mitigate risks like interception or unauthorised access.

  • Privileged Access Management (PAM) with integration to Identity Provider solutions shall be used for access to security critical (including network oversight functions) and network management services.

  • Implement Single Sign-On (SSO) and federated access (e.g., SAML) with trusted validation.

  • External-facing IAM components must be isolated, patched promptly, and monitored as high-value targets.

  • For OT-IT integration, push data one-way (OT to IT) and use inspectable protocols (e.g., web application firewalls).

docs.title: User and administrator responsibilities
docs.text:
• Users must safeguard their identities, report anomalies, and comply with authentication requirements.

  • Administrators must enforce policies, use separate accounts for privileged tasks, and avoid untrusted devices for sensitive operations.

  • Identified staff shall receive training on IAM best practices upon onboarding and annually.

docs.title: Regulatory requirements
docs.text:
• Identities for security critical functions must use unique credentials, MFA, and segregation (Regulation 8(2)(b-c), 8(5)).

  • Remote access is restricted to managed devices via jump boxes (Regulation 3(3)(a),(d),(e), 3(5)).

  • Risks from third-party identities are assessed (Regulation 7(1)), with logging of all access (Code of Practice para 3.4-3.7).

docs.title: Document Objective
docs.text:
This Privileged Access Rights Policy establishes requirements for managing privileged access rights at Community Fibre Limited to protect critical information assets and infrastructure. It supports the overarching ISP034-Access Control Policy by detailing controls for privileged access, while complementing other supporting policies such as the ISP011 -- Information Access Rights Policy, ISP040-Password Management Policy, ISP012-Identity Management Policy, and ISP014-User Registration Policy.

This policy aligns with NCSC guidance on privileged access management and secure privileged access workstations (Use privileged access management - NCSC.GOV.UK), and addresses regulatory requirements, including The Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022.

This document meets the following clauses:

  • ISO/IEC 27001:2022 -- A.5.16: Identity management

  • The Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022 -- Regulation 8 (Access controls for security-critical functions) and Code of Practice (3.1--3.7)

docs.title: Scope and principles
docs.text:
This policy applies to all privileged access rights, including administrative, root, or elevated privileges used to manage business systems, network appliances, network management infrastructure, applications, and other information assets at Community Fibre. It covers employees, contractors, third parties, and system accounts with privileged capabilities, throughout the asset lifecycle.

Key principles:

{width="0.6666666666666666in" height="0.6666666666666666in"}

  • Grant only necessary privileges, separate from standard user activities.

  • Continuously verify and validate privileged access.

  • Use control proportionate to asset sensitivity (ISP037-Information Classification and Handling Policy).

  • Provide temporary, task-specific privileges. (Just-In-Time (JIT) and Just-Enough-Administration (JEA))

  • Use dedicated devices and monitoring to isolate high-risk activities.

  • Log, audit, and review all privileged actions.

Privileged access is managed by Security Operations, Network Technology and IT Service Desk, with oversight from the ISMS Board.

docs.title: Identification and classification of privileged access
docs.text:
• Privileged access is identified through risk assessments and classifying and grouping administration into tiers:

  • Tier 0 - root of trust that all other administration relies upon, examples include:

    • Root domain administrators that can create additional, highly privileged accounts.

    • The root account in a cloud service, that manages the privileges of all other accounts.

    • Infrastructure that is used to generate cryptographic material which other components rely upon.

  • Tier 1 - infrastructure used to carry out highly privileged functions on critical systems, but more constrained than tier 0, examples include:

    • Administrators of a critical database used to store a large amount of sensitive information.

    • Infrastructure that is used for network management or oversight functions.

    • The ability to control and manage critical services in a cloud environment.

  • Tier 2 - infrastructure used to carry out privileged functions, but over a small number of components, impact of compromise is limited, require extra effort from attackers needing full compromise to succeed, example include:

    • Administrator access on an important business support application.

    • Root level access on a front-end web server that forms part of a wider cloud architecture.

    • Administration of a dashboard responsible for monitoring network infrastructure.

  • Tier 3 - infrastructure that allows a constrained set of functions over a single or small number of components, impact of compromise in this tier not catastrophic to business operations, examples include:

    • First line support staff issuing a password reset.

    • The ability to trigger a predefined action in a cloud environment, such as promotion of new feature code into a live environment.

    • Modification of values in systems that are bound by limits set by a component or administrator in a lower tier.

docs.title: Granting and managing privileged access rights
docs.text:
• Requests for privileged access must be submitted via IT Service Desk, with explicit approval from the asset owner and either Network Technology management or Security Operations, based on business need and risk.

  • Use RBAC integrated with Identity Providers (per ISP041) for automated provisioning; apply JIT/JEA for temporary elevations.

  • Privileged accounts must be separate from standard user accounts, no reuse of credentials across systems.

  • Passwords and secrets must follow ISP040-Password Management Policy, stored in secure vaults (e.g., Bitwarden), with automated rotation (e.g., 30 days for Tier 0).

  • MFA is mandatory for all privileged access; prohibit hardcoded credentials.

  • Reviews occur every 6 months or upon changes, revoking unnecessary privileges immediately.

docs.title: Privileged access workstations (PAWs)
docs.text:
• High-risk privileged access (e.g., Tier 0/1) must use dedicated, hardened physical PAWs isolated from general productivity tasks.

  • Must be implemented in alignment with NCSC\'s principles for PAWs:

  • Periodic risk assessments to define scope, including which roles and systems that require PAWs.

  • Must be practical and support administrative tasks without compromising security.

  • Must be built on trusted, verified hardware and software baselines, supplied via trusted suppliers, support and use secure boot processes, standardise on hardened operating systems (e.g., Windows with latest security features) and verified through integrity checks and regular patching.

  • Must use automated provisioning and configuration, defined as code. PAW administrators must be limited to authorised staff, no user outside of this group should be able to make changes. PAW controls must only be managed from another PAW device.

  • PAW devices should be configured to meet administrative access needs only; corporate applications must be blocked. Access to external services must be restricted to the services that are essential for it to operate. All communication should be established outbound from the PAW to the systems and devices it manages. Any unnecessary application or functionality must be disabled or removed.

  • If local virtualisation is used, connectivity between the guest and host OS must be limited. Virtualisation features such as clipboard and file sharing should be limited. The need for local admin rights on the PAW should be limited and designed away, leveraging virtualisation if needed.

  • Monitoring must provide visibility over both the systems that support and configure the PAW devices, as well as the PAW's. Additional monitoring of privileged accounts must be in place to detect anomalies.

  • Data flows to and from the PAW environment must be controlled, access to corporate data file-sharing services must be restricted. Transfers must be limited to approved data types, complex data types like Word and PDF files should not be used. Audit trails should be produced for all data entering and leaving PAW environments, and data must be inspected for malicious content.

  • Privileged access provided to third-party suppliers requires a physical PAW device which complies with Community Fibre's polices on PAWs.

  • Third-party access must be authenticated through Community Fibre's identity provider services.

docs.title: Monitoring, auditing, and session management
docs.text:
• All privileged sessions must be controlled, monitored, and recorded (e.g., video/keystrokes for high-risk), isolated from user workstations.

  • Logs linked to unique identities ISP012-Identity Management Policy, analysed for anomalies; enable session replay for investigations.

  • Protective monitoring detects compromises; audit logs reviewed regularly.

docs.title: Break glass and emergency access
docs.text:
• Critical systems must have at least two break glass accounts, independent of main authentication, with passwords changed after use.

  • Usage triggers notifications, full audits, and incident response.

docs.title: User and administrator responsibilities
docs.text:
• Privileged users must use separate accounts for elevated tasks, report anomalies, and avoid untrusted devices.

  • Complete specialised training on privileged access risks and controls annually.

docs.title: Regulatory requirements
docs.text:
• Privileged access to security-critical functions uses unique credentials, MFA, PAWs, and segregation (Reg 8(2) (b-c), 8(5) [2]).

  • Remote access via jump boxes only (Reg 4(5) [2]); assess third-party risks (Reg 11(b) [2]).

  • Logging and monitoring align with Code of Practice (para 3.4-3.7 [2]).

docs.title: Consequences of non-compliance
docs.text: Any non-compliance with or breach of this policy may lead to investigation and action in line with the organisational Disciplinary Policy (Community Fibre - Employee Handbook 2023 - v3.pdf).

docs.title: Document Objective
docs.text:
This User Registration Policy outlines the requirements for registering and de-registering users at Community Fibre Limited, ensuring secure onboarding and offboarding to protect information assets. It supports the overarching ISP010-Access Control Policy by focusing on user registration and de-registration processes and complements other supporting policies such as theISP011 -- Information Access Rights Policy , ISP040-Password Management Policy, ISP012-Identity Management Policy, and ISP013 -- Privileged Access Rights Policy.

This policy ensures alignment with business needs, information security risks, and regulatory requirements, including the Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022 and its associated Code of Practice.

This document meets the following clauses:

  • Information Security Management System ISO/IEC 27001:2022 -- A.5.16: Identity management (user registration aspects)

  • The Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022 -- Regulation 8: Access controls for security-critical functions, including unique credentials and verification

docs.title: Scope and principles
docs.text:
This policy applies to the registration and de-registration of all users, including employees, contractors, third parties, and system/service accounts, who require access to Community Fibre\'s information assets, networks, systems, and services. It covers the full user lifecycle and aligns with joiners, movers, and leavers processes.

Key principles:

  • Every user must be assigned a unique identifier for accountability.

  • Registration controls are proportionate to the level of access and asset sensitivity (per ISP037-Information Classification and Handling Policy).

  • Initial access is minimal, based on role and need-to-know.

  • Use automation for efficient, error-free registration (ISP012-Identity Management Policy).

  • Ensure immediate removal of access upon departure or change to prevent unauthorised use.

  • All processes are auditable and aligned with legal and regulatory obligations.

User registration is managed by HR, IT Service Desk, and Security Operations, with oversight from the ISMS Board.

docs.title: User registration process
docs.text:
• Registration is initiated by a formal request from an authorised manager or HR for employees, or via contracts for contractors/third parties.

  • The process includes:

  • Obtaining full name, role, contact information, and justification for access.

  • Assignment of a unique user ID, linked to the individual\'s identity (ISP012-Identity Management Policy).

  • Initial access provisioning based on RBAC, aligned with job role and least privilege (ISP011 -- Information Access Rights Policy).

  • Issuance of authentication information, such as temporary passwords or MFA setup (ISP040-Password Management Policy).

  • For privileged access, additional approvals and controls apply (per ISP013 -- Privileged Access Rights Policy).

  • Users must acknowledge acceptance of policies (e.g., ISP030-Acceptable Use Policy.pdf, Code of Conduct) and complete security awareness training within a reasonable timeframe after activation.

  • Automated tools (e.g., integration with Microsoft Entra ID) are used for provisioning to ensure consistency and speed.

docs.title: Verification and authentication
docs.text:
• Identity verification is required prior to registration:

  • HR verifies via background checks, ID documents, and right-to-work confirmation.

  • Contracts, NDAs/DPAs, and supplier risk assessments must be completed.

  • Basic for Public/Confidential assets; enhanced (e.g., security vetting) for Strictly Confidential or privileged access.

  • Authentication setup includes:

  • Unique, non-guessable credentials; no defaults.

  • MFA enablement for remote or sensitive access.

  • Risk-based checks (e.g., behavioural analytics) during initial login.

  • Temporary credentials must be changed immediately upon first use.

docs.title: User de-registration process
docs.text:
• De-registration is triggered immediately by HR notifications (e.g., termination) or security incidents.

  • The process includes:

  • Revocation of all access rights and credentials (ISP011 -- Information Access Rights Policy).

  • Disablement or deletion of user IDs (ISP012-Identity Management Policy).

  • Return or secure disposal of company assets (e.g., devices, badges).

  • Automated de-provisioning where integrated; manual steps logged and confirmed.

  • Dormant accounts (inactive for 90 days) are automatically disabled and reviewed for permanent removal.

  • Post-de-registration audits ensure no residual access remains.

docs.title: Third-party and contractor registration
docs.text:
• Third-party users follow the same processes but with additional controls:

  • Registration requires NDA and approved contracts and specifying access scope, duration, and monitoring.

  • Access is time-bound and limited to specific systems/assets.

  • Remote access restricted to jump boxes or managed devices; UK-based where possible.

  • Regular reviews (e.g., quarterly) to confirm ongoing need.

  • Risks from third parties are assessed and mitigated (e.g., via DPAs for PII handling).v

docs.title: Monitoring and review
docs.text:
• All registration and de-registration activities are logged by the IT Service Desk.

  • Periodic reviews (at least every 6 months) validate active users against business needs.

**

docs.title: Regulatory requirements
docs.text:
• User registration for security-critical functions ensures unique credentials, verification, and segregation (Regulation 8(2) (b-c), 8(5)).

  • Remote access is restricted to managed devices (Regulation 4(5)).

  • Third-party risks are assessed (Regulation 11(b)), with logging of registrations (Code of Practice para 3.4-3.7).

  • Training includes competency on access controls (Regulation 13(2)(a)).
